**Fitted under the reading, the best family ends where it stood under the readout.** Three fits were then made with the reading in the loss, in the APL-effect term and in the response-rate terms alike. The breadth-2 family and the same family with the firing ceiling at the literature setting end level, each a little below its start (first two rows of the table), at the loss that the breadth-2 fit has under the readout; the reference model's set with the ceiling does not move and stays behind. The pattern part is where it was (fourth row; {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit under the readout), far above its floor, and ρ on the per-pair APL effect is no nearer its ceiling. What differs between the two fits of the family is how they hold under the other definitions. The fit without the ceiling got its loss with a somatic threshold still further below the baseline's ({{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of it, from {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}}) and a stronger APL→KC ({{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, from {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}}), and it is worse than its start on raw counts and under the readout; the fit with the ceiling scores about the same under all three definitions (sixth row). Through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), the trials read through the reading, the order turns (seventh row). The fit without the ceiling improves, at the noise matched to APL output blocked (TNT) as well ({{E73/partB/zcell_noise.csv:model=E73-zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3;level=match_off;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}), and the fit with the ceiling worsens ({{E73/partB/zcell_noise.csv:model=E73-zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_off;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} there), because the noise lowers its mean effect, as it does for the fit with the ceiling made before ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating_trials;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} through the noise, from {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} without it). The margin between the two is about twice what one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss under the readout ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), on one seed of the noise and on the real wiring only. Under the reading the firing ceiling is thus no better than the family without it, and its case for joining the base model rests on raw counts and on realism (bounded spike counts, the spread of an odor's response over its KCs), not on this reading. On raw counts the case has since narrowed to single wirings and to the model without noise: as a mean over wirings read through the trial noise the two families are level ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile), at the end of this section).

**What the normalization had hidden.** In the flies a KC's unit grows with the number of odors the KC responds to ([the footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the ratios), so that the responders' mean amplitude, about {{data:ctrl_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .0f}} z whatever the KC's breadth, is in baseline-noise units nearly twice as large in the control flies' KCs that respond to eight odors as in those that respond to one (the last row but one of the table; few KCs respond to exactly eight odors with APL on, in the flies and in the models, so the values at eight are rough). The flat amplitude in z is strongly growing responses compressed by the normalization. The models' responses grow much less: read the same way, their responders' amplitudes in baseline-noise units start lower and rise by a half to two thirds, their units hardly grow (the row above it), and with the firing ceiling both are lower still. The models' responses fill their sessions much less than the flies' do, so in the amplitudes the models are further from the flies than the comparison in z had said ([the low end of the readout](#readout) made it in z). The realism bands hold a model to which KCs respond, not to how strongly, and do not see this.

**The response criterion, and the realism bands.** Read this way a model is held to the flies' own criterion, a response above 1 z in a unit that belongs to each KC, in place of two or more spikes. Every model of the table then has fewer responses with APL off than it has at two spikes (the two rows on the response rates), and its distribution of odors per KC with APL off is nearer the flies' (the three rows on odors per KC). The current reference model and its set with the ceiling, outside the band when their two-spike responses are set against the flies' responses above 1 z, are inside it once both sides are counted above 1 z: the flag had belonged to the comparison, a fixed criterion on one side against one that grows with how much a KC responds on the other, and not to the models. That was the comparison of the realism bands. They now count the flies' responses in baseline-noise units and the models' at two or more spikes, a fixed unit on each side, and the per-KC reading is reported beside them without deciding any, because its calibration sets the response rate with APL on whatever the model's firing ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units) has the change, the reasons for it and what it does to the flies' values).

**Realism, and the limits of the reading.** The three fits are inside all four realism bands (last row). Their response-rate terms were under the reading, whose calibration sets the response rate with APL on at every evaluation, so nothing in the loss held the number of KCs that fire. These fits moved their two-spike response rates little (the fit without the ceiling ends with {{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_k2_cap3:rate_ratio_off_over_on ~ .2f}} times as many responses with APL off as with APL on, inside the band, against the flies' {{data:noise_rate_ratio_fraction ~ .2f}}), but [a later fit made the same way left its operating point](#apl-effect-by-class), and fits now keep their response-rate terms on the two-spike count. The reading has no calcium kinetics: a model's response is confined to its window, {{data:zcell_q_window ~ .0%}} of the recording, where the recordings' own edge implies {{data:zcell_q ~ .0%}}, the responses outlasting their windows. At that share the breadth-2 fit's loss under the reading is {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading_def=zcell_saturating_q0.180;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}} in place of the first row's value, and the fit with the ceiling made before hardly moves ({{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating_q0.180;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}, from the second row's {{E73/key_models.csv:folder=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;reading_def=zcell_saturating;reading=graded:rmse ~ .3f}}). The drift and the measurement noise are one value for every model KC, where they differ between the flies' KCs. The criterion does not account for the missing responses at [low concentration](#low-concentration) either: read within the session of its own panel, the current reference model has {{E73/low_conc.csv:model=ref40_68;map=saturating;panel=diag_mix;condition=on;odor=ma @ -7:frac_zcell ~ .1%}} of its KCs responding to ma @ -7 with APL on, as at two spikes, against {{E73/low_conc.csv:model=ref40_68;map=saturating;panel=diag_mix;condition=on;odor=ma @ -7:frac_data ~ .1%}} in the flies. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### Which KCs carry the APL effect: the effect split by the number of odors each KC responds to {#apl-effect-by-class}

**Split by how many of the 16 odors a KC responds to, with a response counted as the recordings count it, above 1 z, the flies' APL effect rests on broadly responding KCs of two kinds, the few that respond to eight or more odors when APL output is blocked and the many that respond to four to seven. The models make theirs with the first kind alone, in every best fit and on every wiring. The difference belongs to that unit: with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the flies' effect, too, sits in the KCs at eight or more odors alone (the data side of the main target, at the end of this section). In the z-scored units it is real, and it is not where the pattern error is: across the saved models a split closer to the flies' does not go with a lower pattern part, and a fit that is asked for the flies' split pays for it on the total.** [The input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold) left open which KCs carry the effect, in the flies and in the models. A pair's cosine similarity is a sum over KCs (the sum that [the low end of the readout](#readout) divided by whether its two entries are responses), so the per-pair APL effect can be divided among groups of KCs. The APL effect split by odors per KC put every KC, in each condition, in one of the five groups of the realism band on odors per KC, by the number of the 16 odors it responds to in that condition (none, one, two or three, four to seven, eight or more; one to three are shown together below), and took each group's part of every pair's similarity. A class's APL effect is its part of the similarity with APL off minus its part with APL on, and the classes' effects add up to the pair's APL effect. A KC can change class between the conditions, so the split says how much of each condition's similarity sits in KCs of a given tuning width; it needs no pairing of cells between the conditions, which the recordings cannot give, the control flies and the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) being different animals. In the recordings a response is a trial mean above 1 z, each genotype's class parts are averaged over its recordings, and the 90 % intervals are over recordings drawn again with replacement. Every archived model with both conditions saved ({{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:n ~ .0f}} variants) was read in two ways: through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) with a response at two or more spikes, and as the recordings are produced, each KC in units of its own standard deviation over the session (the per-KC reading of [the subsection before this one](#per-kc-normalization)), with the recordings' criterion and through that reading's measurement noise, as ten pseudo-recordings of three trials, so that a model KC enters a class as a recorded KC does.

The per-pair APL effect of the KC data split by the number of odors a KC responds to in each condition. A class's share of the variance is the covariance of its effect with the whole effect across the 120 pairs over the variance of the whole effect, so the shares add up to 1; the similarity a class carries is its part of the cosine similarity between two odors, averaged over the 120 pairs

**By the recordings' own criterion the flies' APL effect rests on broadly responding KCs of two kinds.** The KCs that respond to eight or more odors, {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .1%}} of the KCs with APL output blocked (TNT) and almost none in the control flies, carry most of the mean effect and about half of its variance across pairs. Those that respond to four to seven odors, {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_4_7 ~ .1%}} of the KCs with APL output blocked (TNT) against {{data:ctrl_odors_per_kc_4_7 ~ .1%}} in the control flies, carry the rest and a third of the variance. The KCs that respond to one to three odors, two fifths of the KCs in either genotype, add nothing, and those that respond to none take a little away. The third of the mean effect that [the low end of the readout](#readout) found in products of a responder with a sub-threshold entry sits in the same broad KCs (third row): it is their weaker responses to their other odors, not the responses of weakly responding cells. With the response criterion at 0.75 or 1.25 z in place of 1 z the class at four to seven carries {{data:apl_class_effect_4_7_z0.75 ~ +.3f}} or {{data:apl_class_effect_4_7_z1.25 ~ +.3f}} and the class at eight or more {{data:apl_class_effect_8plus_z0.75 ~ +.3f}} or {{data:apl_class_effect_8plus_z1.25 ~ +.3f}}: how the effect divides between the two kinds moves with the criterion and neither changes sign, so a model is compared with the flies at a matched criterion only. The flies therefore do not make the effect through the amplitudes of weak responses in place of broad responders, as the input-scaled KC threshold had read them: flies and models both make it through broad responders, the flies, by this criterion, through two kinds. The second kind belongs to the criterion and its unit. With each KC's responses in baseline-noise units and the one threshold of the realism bands, the KCs at eight or more odors carry {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_8plus ~ +.3f}}, more than the whole mean effect of {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}, and those at four to seven {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7 ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_4_7.hi ~ +.3f}}): there the flies, like the models, make the effect with the broadest KCs alone ([the data side of the main target](#data-side), at the end of this section). What the rest of this subsection says about the class at four to seven is a comparison in the recordings' z-scored units, with both sides counted above 1 z.

A model's split is scored by the class-resolved loss: the root mean square, over the five classes and the 120 pairs, of the model's per-class effect minus the flies' (lower is better). Its floor, a resampled set of recordings scored against the measured one, is {{data:apl_class_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} ({{data:apl_class_rmse_floor.lo ~ .3f}} to {{data:apl_class_rmse_floor.hi ~ .3f}}), and one control recording paired with one recording with APL output blocked (TNT), scored against the mean of the others, has a median of {{data:apl_class_rmse_yardstick ~ .3f}}.

**Counted above 1 z, every best fit lacks the middle class, on every wiring.** In every model of the table but the one with the input-scaled threshold, the KCs at four to seven odors carry between a quarter and three fifths of what they carry in the flies, below the lower end of the data's interval; the KCs at eight or more odors carry the model's whole effect and more, and the KCs at one to three odors take away from it, where in the flies they add nothing. About half of the variance of the fits' pattern error across the pairs is in the class at four to seven, less in the reference model (the row on the pattern error, and the right panel of the figure). Through the calibrated readout, with a response at two or more spikes, the same holds more strongly: in the breadth-2 fit the class at four to seven has an effect of {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and the class at eight or more {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_8plus ~ +.3f}}, at a class-resolved loss of {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:class_rmse ~ .3f}} (left panel of the figure). The shortfall belongs to the family and not to the hemibrain wiring: fitted on each of the eight wirings of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population), the breadth-2 family has the class at four to seven between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} under the per-KC reading, and at {{E74/wirings.csv:group=c2;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} in the mean over the wirings.

**The models' moderately broad KCs are too broad already with APL on.** Under the per-KC reading the similarity that the class at four to seven carries with APL off is within a tenth of the flies' in every model of the table but the one with the input-scaled threshold, and with APL on it is two fifths to three fifths above the control flies', whose 90 % interval is {{E74/data_by_class.csv:criterion=1.0;quantity=level_on;class=4_7;term=total:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E74/data_by_class.csv:criterion=1.0;quantity=level_on;class=4_7;term=total:hi ~ .3f}} (the row on the similarity carried). The class's shortfall in the APL effect is thus an excess with APL on: the KCs that respond to four to seven odors while APL is working carry more of the overlap between odors in the models than in the flies, so that removing APL adds less to them. The class at one to three odors is over with APL on in the same way. Through the calibrated readout the excess with APL on is there as well, and the class is short with APL off besides.

**A split closer to the flies' does not go with a lower pattern part.** If the missing class were what the pattern part of the APL-effect loss is made of, the archived models with a split nearer the flies' would be the ones with a lower pattern part. They are not: across the {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:n ~ .0f}} variants the Spearman correlation between the class-resolved loss and the pattern part is {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=cal2;subset=all variants:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} through the calibrated readout and {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=all variants:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} under the per-KC reading, and across the {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=inside the two-spike bands:n ~ .0f}} of them inside the realism bands {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=cal2;subset=inside the two-spike bands:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}} and {{E74/rank_correlations.csv:reading=zcell;subset=inside the two-spike bands:rho_class_vs_pattern ~ +.2f}}. In the whole archive, under the per-KC reading, the class at four to seven reaches the flies' interval only in models with a per-claw threshold, the claw coincidence rule or the input-scaled KC threshold, and where such a model can be set beside the same family without it, the pattern does not come with the class. The breadth-2 family with a 40 Hz per-claw threshold was fitted on the same five wirings as the family without it ([above](#wiring-population)). Under the per-KC reading it has the class at four to seven higher on every one of them, between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=thr40_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed4_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} against {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} to {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}}, through less of the class's similarity with APL on, and a higher pattern part on every one, between {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=thr40_wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed3_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;tag=wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_pattern ~ .3f}}.

**Asked for the flies' split, the family pays on the total.** The family with the firing ceiling was fitted again from its optimum under the per-KC reading (third model column) with the class-resolved loss added to its loss, weighted so that a fall in it counts about as much as an equal rise in the APL-effect loss (fourth column). The class-resolved loss falls by a fifth, mostly because the class at eight or more odors comes down toward the flies'; the class at four to seven hardly moves, the mean APL effect moves away from the flies', the APL-effect loss rises by {{diff:E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E74_apl_effect_by_odors_per_kc;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse -- E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E73_per_kc_normalization;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse ~ .3f}} and its pattern part stays where it was. No evaluation along the fit lowers the class-resolved loss without raising the APL-effect loss. The family's good totals rest on class errors of opposite sign, too much effect in the KCs at eight or more odors and a loss of effect in those at one to three, that cancel pair by pair, and moving one class toward the flies' unbalances the other. The rise is about what one draw of the wiring moves the loss ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}} under the readout) and the fit was made on the real wiring only, so its size is a single reading; that the pattern part does not fall is what the archive says as well.

**With the input-scaled threshold the family reaches the middle class only by leaving its operating point.** The same experiment made the fit that the input-scaled KC threshold had left as the one to try ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)): the family with the firing ceiling and the threshold scaled at a power of 0.25, fitted under the per-KC reading (fifth model column). Under that reading its APL-effect loss ends {{diff:E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E73_per_kc_normalization;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;reading=zcell:apl_rmse -- E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E74_apl_effect_by_odors_per_kc;tag=zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2;reading=zcell:apl_rmse ~ .3f}} below the fit without the scaling, within a draw of the wiring; its class at four to seven is inside the flies' interval; the KCs with nine or more claws take {{E74/released_by_claws.csv:model=fit S;reading=zcell;group=9+:share_added ~ .0%}} of the responses that removing APL adds, where they take {{E74/released_by_claws.csv:model=reading ceiling;reading=zcell;group=9+:share_added ~ .0%}} without the scaling; and under the recordings' criterion its distribution of odors per KC with APL off is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_zcell_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies', against {{E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_zcell_opk_off_tv ~ .3f}}. It gets there by leaving the model's operating point. In the fits under the per-KC reading the response-rate terms of the loss were computed under the recordings' criterion, and the reading is calibrated at every evaluation to the flies' response rate with APL on, so the number of KCs that fire was free. This fit used the freedom. It weakened the inhibition, APL→KC from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:apl_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} and APL→bouton from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's and the KC–KC scale from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}} to {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}, at a common somatic threshold that stayed near {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's, until its response rate at two or more spikes with APL on is {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}}, from {{E71/fits.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:rate_on ~ .3f}} at its start and against a band of 0.045 to 0.085. Through the calibrated readout and on raw counts it is {{diff:E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_cal_rmse -- E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_apl_cal_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{diff:E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_thrin0.25_k2:fit_apl_raw_rmse -- E73/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcell_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:fit_apl_raw_rmse ~ .3f}} worse than the fit without the scaling, its class-resolved loss is the highest of the table, and its class at four to seven is the difference between two levels that are both above the flies' (the row on the similarity carried). It is a measurement of what that freedom allows, not a candidate base. Fits now keep their response-rate terms on the two-spike criterion, and the per-KC reading is reported beside the realism bands without deciding them ([the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), so the fit that was asked for the flies' split, made under the same rule though inside the bands at its optimum, is likewise a measurement and not a candidate for the best-models table.

**Realism.** The split itself changes no model. Of the two fits made here, the one asked for the flies' split is inside all four bands at its optimum (the last two rows of the table), with a common somatic threshold of {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:thr_factor ~ .2f}} and an APL→bouton scale of {{E74/fits.csv:zcaplrate_rate0.068_aplzcellclslin_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, as hard to defend as in the fits it starts from; the one with the input-scaled threshold is outside three of the bands, as described. The only fit that reached the flies' middle class thus did it outside the bands, and the fit that was asked for the split stayed inside them and paid on the main target. The split counts the flies' responses by the recordings' own criterion of 1 z, and the models' under the per-KC reading by the same criterion, not in the [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units) in which the realism bands count the flies' responses, and in those units the flies have no middle class for a model to reach, their KCs at four to seven odors carrying none of the effect ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)); as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Which KCs carry the effect becomes a statistic of its own, reported for later fits beside the realism bands, and in both units of the flies' responses: counted above 1 z the flies' effect sits in two classes of broadly responding KCs, and a model that has the total right with one of them has it by cancellation, while in baseline-noise units it sits in the broadest class alone, in the flies as in the models ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). It is not a route to a lower pattern part. What is left of the pattern is looked for pair by pair, in the errors that remain whatever the classes do. A mechanism that makes moderately broad KCs less broad with APL on at no cost on the total, which nothing in the archive does, is wanted only if the main target stays in the recordings' z-scored units. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition: whether APL's weight by glomerulus carries the error common to the wirings {#glomerulus-profile}

**The error that every wiring shares is in almost every saved model, and least in a few that change what reaches the KCs, whose own errors are no smaller. A profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, the one rule about which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring, does not carry it: one glomerulus at a time moves the per-pair APL effect little, and a profile over all of them, built from those single changes, lowers the loss on the real wiring and raises the block to the flies' but does not predict the pairs of an odor it was built without. Read as a population of wirings through the trial noise, the family with the firing ceiling is level on raw counts with the family without it.** [The APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) left an error that no draw of the wiring removes, the common error: under the calibrated readout the APL effect of the breadth-2 family is too small among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and too large among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, on every wiring. A draw changes which KC has which claws and keeps the glomeruli, so a rule written per glomerulus is the one way to say which KCs APL acts on that is the same on every wiring. The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition asked whether such a rule carries the common error. A profile is one score per glomerulus by which APL's weight is multiplied, at one of three sites: the cell (a KC's whole APL weight, once for each claw it has from the glomerulus), the claw (the weight on the claws from the glomerulus) or the bouton (the weight on the glomerulus's boutons), with the mean factor held at 1. Everything was run on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring (the first model column of the first table [above](#wiring-population)), at its fitted parameters. At every point the APL scale was set again so that the number of responses with APL on stayed the fit's, and the run with APL off is the fit's own, since APL's weights do nothing there. Values are through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named: under it the fit has the flies' mean effect, and its loss is nearly all pattern.

**The common error is in almost every saved model.** For each of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_variants:value ~ .0f}} saved variants with both conditions, the part of its own pattern error that lies along the common error was measured as a projection: 1 if the variant has as much of the common error as the mean over the eight wirings has, 0 if it has none. Under the readout the median is {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_cal_proj_common:value ~ .2f}} (on raw counts {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_median_raw_proj_common:value ~ .2f}}): the error is older than the best family and belongs to nothing particular to it. Only {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_cal_proj_below_0.5:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:archive_n_variants_cal:value ~ .0f}} variants scored under the readout carry less than half of it. Two are settings of the oracle co-responder suppression, which is told which KCs to take out. The others change what reaches the KCs: four settings of a weaker antennal-lobe normalization, which passes more of the ORNs' contrast on to the PNs, on the early hemibrain model with one unit per KC and no separate claws (down to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd10000:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}; that model as it is carries {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd31.4088:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); Hallem's receptor data alone as the input for ms, paa, B-myr and 1-8ol ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E38_hallem_input;tag=B_thr70_gain1.5_k2_cap3_hallem_only:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); the lowest two of the random wirings of that early model ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E4_substrate;tag=uniform_sp0.05_seed9:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}} and {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E4_substrate;tag=hemidraw_sp0.05_seed4:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}); and a 130 Hz per-claw threshold followed by a cap on each claw's input ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E16_claw_saturation;tag=bouton_thr130_tanh50:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}). APL's inhibition of the PN boutons scaled down or up, by contrast, leaves the common error where it was ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=bouton_pnapl_x1:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}} to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=bouton_pnapl_x2:cal_proj_common ~ .2f}}). None of these eight has a smaller pattern part than the breadth-2 fit ({{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E3_drive_dependent_gain;tag=hemibrain-wd20_inhadd10000:cal_err_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E75/archive_vs_common_error.csv:folder=E16_claw_saturation;tag=bouton_thr130_tanh50:cal_err_rms ~ .3f}}, against {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}): they carry a different error, not a smaller one.

**One glomerulus at a time moves little.** With APL's weight doubled on one glomerulus, for each of the 36 glomeruli with ORN input at each of the three sites, the loss stays between {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_x2_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_x2_cal_loss_max:value ~ .3f}}; with the weight halved, on the eight glomeruli per site whose doubling had moved the effect most, between {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_max:value ~ .3f}}. The fit's own loss is {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and the floor {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}, so the best single change gains {{diff:E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss -- E75/report_scalars.csv:map_half_cal_loss_min:value ~ .3f}}. Nor do glomeruli changed together add up: a set of four or eight changed at once moves the per-pair effect by well under the sum of its members' single changes.

**A profile fitted through the single changes fails the test set for it.** For each site, scores for all 36 glomeruli (ridge-penalized, no factor beyond four either way) were fitted so that the single changes, added up, cancel the common error. The test was fixed before the fit and had two parts. Fitted without one odor, a profile had to remove 15 % or more of the common error's squared sum on that odor's 15 pairs. Fitted to the effect of one half of the recordings, it had to lower the error against the other half in 90 of 100 random splits.

The profiles fitted through the single-glomerulus changes, by the site at which they act: the share of the common error's squared sum that the added-up changes remove, and the splits of the recordings won

No site passes both parts. The claw and the bouton fail both. The cell, alone or with the claw, passes the first and fails the second, and that failure is in the recordings: two of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) have much lower distances than the other six, and the cell profile wins {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_apart_won:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_apart_n:value ~ .0f}} splits that put those two in different halves and {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_together_won:value ~ .0f}} of the {{E75/report_scalars.csv:split_cell_together_n:value ~ .0f}} that put both in one. A half with both and a half with neither are different targets, so this part of the test measured the recordings more than the profile; what the two recordings do to the target is in [the data side of the main target](#data-side), the next subsection: they are stronger than the other six and not different in pattern, and the mean over all eight stands.

**Simulated, the cell profile helps the real wiring and not a left-out odor.** By the plan a failed test closed the experiment. Because the failed part had read the recordings, and both parts rested on single changes that do not add up, the cell profile was simulated all the same, as a diagnostic in stages that kept the test's thresholds. Of the strengths tried, half its scores (every factor at its square root) is the one at which its change takes away the largest share of the common error: were the change it makes on the real wiring the same on every wiring, {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage1_transfer_x0.5:value ~ .0%}} of it (15 % was asked), where the same scores permuted across the glomeruli would add to the error (two draws). The next stage failed. The sixteen profiles each fitted without one odor, simulated at the same strength and scored on that odor's pairs, remove {{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_pooled_heldout:value ~ .1%}} of the common error there, pooled, against the 15 % asked and the {{E75/profile_cv.csv:profile=cell;variant=ridge:loo_odor_reduction ~ .1%}} that the added-up changes had predicted. They help most for B-myr, IaA, pa and paa ({{E75/report_scalars.csv:d2_stage2_fold_B-myr:value ~ .0%}} of the common error on B-myr's pairs) and add to the error for 6al, t2h, 2-but and -aPine. The splits of the recordings with the two recordings kept apart did not run, and neither did the fits with a profile on several wirings, for which the test was the gate. A fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, found by adding up single-glomerulus changes, therefore does not carry the common error. The result goes no further than that: scores fitted directly in simulation, on several wirings at once, were not tried, nor was APL inhibition that depends on the odor at the scale of a bouton (one form of it, inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input, has since been emulated and does not lower the pattern part: [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side); another, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, removes too little of the common error on left-out odors as a proxy on the input: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps)).

**On the real wiring the profile lowers the loss and makes the block.** At half its scores the cell profile lowers the fit's loss by {{diff:E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:cal_loss -- E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, about what one draw of the wiring moves this family's loss ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and all of it in the pattern part: ρ on the per-pair APL effect rises, both group errors shrink, and the block under the readout, which a block term in the loss had not raised in this fit ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)), comes to the flies' (first six rows). The same scores permuted leave the loss where it was or raise it ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_perm1_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_perm2_x0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}}). The mean effect falls a little, and on raw counts, where it was short already, the loss rises (seventh row). At the full scores the loss is the same ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_loss ~ .3f}}), with a lower pattern part ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}), a larger block ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x1:cal_block ~ +.3f}}) and a smaller mean effect, and at twice the scores it is above the fit's ({{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x2:cal_loss ~ .3f}}). The doubled four do half as much for the loss and as much for the block. These are gains on one wiring. Neither change was run on a re-drawn wiring, and the left-out odors say what the profile's gain is: 36 scores fitted to these 120 pairs, not a rule that holds for the pairs of an odor it was fitted without.

**With flies and trials both in the model, the firing ceiling's lead on raw counts is gone.** The same experiment made the check that the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings had left open ([above](#wiring-population)): the family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting, on the four wirings it has been fitted on (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), read through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) and then averaged over the wirings, as the family without a ceiling had been.

Without noise the mean over the four wirings with the ceiling is far below the mean without it; through the noise the two are level, apart by well under what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The noise raises the mean APL effect of the family without the ceiling and lowers that of the family with it, to nearly the same value, short of the flies' (third and fourth rows), and the pattern parts are the same (last row). On each of the four wirings singly the fit with the ceiling is still the lower one through the noise (between {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} and {{E75/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} at the noise matched to the control flies, against {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-curveball_within_type_matched-seed1_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E72/partE_noise.csv:group=E72-wiring-claw_permutation_within_type-seed2_rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} without it, the last column of the second table [above](#wiring-population)): averaging over wirings helps the family without the ceiling more. Read as the data are made, a mean over flies and over trials, the ceiling thus gives no clear gain on raw counts, as it gave none under the per-KC reading ([above](#per-kc-normalization)); its lead there belongs to the model without noise and to single wirings, and what it adds beyond that is realism, bounded spike counts and the spread of an odor's response over its KCs. The trial noise of this reading is all shared between the odors of a trial, where only part of the flies' is. Re-specified to the flies' shares it gives {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} without the ceiling and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} with it, apart by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, so the reading holds ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)).

**Realism.** A profile acts only with APL on, and every point keeps the fit's number of responses there, so the response rates, their ratio and everything with APL off are the fit's own; what a profile can change is which odors keep their responses with APL on. With the half-strength profile and with the doubled four the response rate ρ with APL on rises and the distribution of odors per KC stays where it was, and both are inside all four bands, counted as the bands count now and as they did until 2026-11-10 (lower rows of the table on the real wiring). The profile's scores stay well inside the factor of four allowed. One point of the single-glomerulus runs left a band: four times the weight at the boutons of the eight glomeruli of the block-specific set of the breadth × shared-input APL rule took the response rate ρ with APL on to {{E75/report_points.csv:bouton_E15_eight_x4:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} (by the recordings' own criterion; its responses were not saved), and no later stage used it. Which KCs carry the effect does not change either: through the calibrated readout, with a response at two or more spikes, the mean per-pair APL effect carried by the KCs that respond to four to seven odors is {{E75/report_points.csv:D2s1_cell_ridge_x0.5:class_eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} with the half-strength profile and {{E75/sensitivity_map.csv:base:class_eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} without it ([the APL effect split by odors per KC](#apl-effect-by-class)). What the bands do not see is the fit's as well: the release through the many-claw KCs when APL is removed, a somatic threshold under half the baseline's and an APL→bouton scale near its bound ([above](#wiring-population)). As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), so the scores of the glomeruli that mainly carry those odors are in part scores for a mismatched input.

**What follows.** The common error stays the target. APL's fixed targeting by glomerulus is left without support as its source in this family, though not excluded, and the per-odor APL oracle had already shown that how many KCs APL removes for each odor does not set the pattern ([above](#apl-effect-parts)). The few saved models with little of the common error all change what reaches the KCs. They carry a different error, not a smaller one, so they say where to look and not what works, and that is where the next mechanisms were looked for: in the best family no fixed change of the input carries the common error either ([the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), at the end of this section). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The data side of the main target: the unit of the flies' responses, the recordings one by one, and fits to the effect in baseline-noise units {#data-side}

**The unit in which each KC's responses are taken moves the mean of the flies' APL effect and not its pattern. In baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, the mean effect is about a third larger than in the recordings' z-scored units, the pattern across pairs is the same within its floor, and the saved models keep their order on raw counts. In those units the KCs that respond to eight or more odors carry the flies' effect alone. The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that stand apart from the other six are stronger and not different, so the mean over all eight stands as the target, and neither a weaker APL nor a shifted somatic threshold makes their state in the model. Fitted to the effect in baseline-noise units, the family with the firing ceiling raises its mean effect by more than half of what was missing, at a cost on the pattern and with more broad responders, and read through the trial noise it keeps little of the gain.** Every loss elsewhere on this page is against the flies' per-pair APL effect computed from the recordings as they were made, each KC's trace z-scored over its whole recording. That unit grows with how much a KC responds, which is why the realism bands now count the flies' responses in baseline-noise units ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)); the target itself stayed on the z-scored values, and what the choice of unit does to it was not known. Nor was it known what the target owes to two of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), whose distances are much lower than those of the other six and through which a test on split halves of the recordings had failed ([the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile)). The data side of the main target measured both from the recordings and the saved models: the effect in every unit the recordings allow, every saved model scored against it, and the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) taken one by one. It then moved the model along its own two axes, the strength of APL's output and the somatic threshold, to see whether either makes what sets the two recordings apart, and fitted the best family to the effect in baseline-noise units.

**The unit moves the mean and not the pattern.** The per-pair APL effect was computed again with each KC's trial means in baseline-noise units, as the raw change of the KC's signal, and as that change divided by the KC's mean fluorescence, by its mean signal or by each trial's signal before the odor. Every one of these units gives a larger mean effect than the z-scored values, between {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:mean ~ +.3f}} and {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} against {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} (figure, left): the z-score divides a KC's responses by a spread that its own responses enlarge, and the KCs that respond most carry the effect. The pattern hardly moves. Across the 120 pairs, ρ on the per-pair APL effect between each of these units and the z-scored one is {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fctrial;values=graded:rho_ref ~ .2f}} to {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:rho_ref ~ .2f}}, and with both means removed the two effects differ by a root mean square of {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fcmean;values=graded:pattern_diff_ref ~ .3f}} to {{E76/data_units.csv:unit=dff_fctrial;values=graded:pattern_diff_ref ~ .3f}}, less than the floor of the pattern part (figure, middle). In every unit the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms have a larger effect than the mean over all pairs and the pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al a smaller one, the two groups of the common error. The floor of the loss, the floor of its pattern part and the ceiling on ρ on the per-pair APL effect are nearly the same in the two units (table). The saved models follow: scored on raw counts against the effect in baseline-noise units, the {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:n ~ .0f}} saved variants with both conditions keep the order they have against the z-scored effect, with a Spearman correlation of {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}} between the two losses and {{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=raw;unit=noise;part=pattern;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}} between the two pattern parts. What changes is the mean part, which grows for every model, since no saved model's mean effect on raw counts reaches the flies' in these units. Under [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), calibrated again in the same units, the pattern parts keep their order as well ({{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=cal;unit=noise;part=pattern;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}}) and the losses less closely ({{E76/rank_correlations_units.csv:readout=cal;unit=noise;part=loss;variants=all:spearman ~ .2f}}). The mean part of the APL-effect loss is thus set by a choice on the data's side, and the pattern part is not.

**In baseline-noise units the broadest KCs carry the effect alone.** The split of the effect by the number of odors a KC responds to ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)) does depend on the unit, because the unit decides what counts as a response. With a response counted above 1 z the flies' effect sat in two classes, the KCs that respond to eight or more odors and those that respond to four to seven. With a response counted above the one threshold of baseline-noise units, the first class carries the whole effect and a little more, and the second carries nothing, its 90 % interval holding zero (seventh and eighth rows of the table; figure, right). The two kinds of broad responders of that subsection are therefore a reading in the recordings' z-scored units, in which a KC's unit grows with how much it responds. In the units the realism bands use, the flies make the effect as the models do: read through the calibrated readout with a response at two or more spikes, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit has {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_8plus ~ +.3f}} in the class at eight or more odors and {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_4_7 ~ +.3f}} in the class at four to seven. What still differs is below the broadest class: the model's classes at four to seven and at one to three odors both take from its effect (the second {{E74/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3;reading=cal2:eff_1_3 ~ +.3f}}), where the flies' class at four to seven carries nothing and their KCs at one odor and at two or three odors carry {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_1 ~ +.3f}} and {{data:noise_apl_effect_class_2_3 ~ +.3f}}.

**The two strongest recordings are stronger, not different.** The recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) differ among themselves in level far more than the control flies' do. In the z-scored units, as in the rest of this paragraph unless the other unit is named, two of them have mean distances of {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} and {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT two:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, where the other six have {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT six:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}} and the control recordings {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_min ~ .2f}} to {{E76/recording_ranges.csv:genotype=TNT3c:mean_dist_z_max ~ .2f}}, and the effect computed against the two alone is more than twice the effect against the six (tenth row). A first look had found that the step from the six to the two has another pattern across pairs than the step from the control flies to the six, the ρ between the two steps being near zero. Set against the other ways of splitting the recordings, that is not a difference. Any split of the eight into six and two pulls this ρ negative, because the six's mean enters the two steps with opposite signs; the actual split ranks {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:rank_rho_steps ~ .0f}} of the {{E76/axis_tests.csv:reading=z;genotype=TNT:n_splits ~ .0f}} splits, counted from the lowest, and the two recordings' own steps from the six agree with each other more than two recordings do in most splits (eleventh and twelfth rows; figure below). The same holds in baseline-noise units and with each recording's cosine corrected for trial-to-trial noise (by the correction then in use, which is too low in the level of the distances: [the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The two are unusual in their level alone, and what makes them strong is the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, which blocking APL output brings far closer in them: the effect over those 15 pairs is {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=two:ester ~ +.3f}} against the two and {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=six:ester ~ +.3f}} against the six. Nothing recorded with the flies sets the two apart beforehand, neither the time since the toxin was induced nor the number of KCs. Within the session one thing does: the response rates of the other six run down over the three repeats and those of the two do not ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). The mean over all eight therefore stands as the target, and the failed test on split halves is as it was read, a half with both of the two recordings and a half with neither being different in level. The common error is not made by the two either: against the six alone it has the root mean square it has against all eight ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:rms ~ .3f}} and {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:rms ~ .3f}}) and the same sign in both groups of pairs, with about half of its part among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al gone ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=six_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}} against {{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_z:err_alcohol ~ +.3f}}), and against the effect in baseline-noise units it is as large ({{E76/common_error_subsets_summary.csv:target=eight_noise:rms ~ .3f}}).

![Each recording with APL output blocked (TNT) against the control flies' mean (Yang's z in the panels is the recordings' z-scored unit). Left: each recording's APL effect, the mean over the 120 pairs with the standard deviation across pairs (triangles: the means over the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and over the pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al; orange: the two strongest recordings), in z-scored units (top) and in baseline-noise units (bottom). Right: ρ across the 120 pairs between the step from the control flies to six recordings and the step from those six to the other two, for every split of the eight recordings into six and two (top), and between the two left-out recordings' own steps (bottom); the diamond is the actual split.](results/E76_data_side_target/E76_recordings.png)

**The model's own axes do not make the two recordings.** If the two were flies in which the toxin blocked more of APL's output, or whose KCs were more excitable, a model could make their state by itself. Two models were moved along both axes at fixed parameters, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting as fitted again here (second model column of the table below): APL's output to the KCs and to the boutons scaled to three quarters, a half, a quarter and an eighth with its inputs unchanged, and the somatic threshold shifted by a tenth and by a fifth either way, with APL on and with APL off. Neither axis reaches the two. APL removed altogether is the most that a block can give, a mean effect of {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E67_apl_effect_fits;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the two models on raw counts against the two recordings' {{E76/subset_floors.csv:unit=z;subset=two:mean ~ +.3f}}, and a threshold a fifth higher or lower with APL off leaves the second model's between {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=thr_off;point=thr1.2_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}} and {{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=thr_off;point=thr0.8_off:effect_mean ~ +.3f}}. The last step of the block in that model, from an eighth of APL's output to none, agrees with the flies' step from the six to the two at ρ={{E76/model_axes.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;axis=block;point=base_off:step_rho_step2_z ~ .2f}} across the 120 pairs, as well as the two recordings agree with each other, but it ends at the level of all eight recordings and not of the two; no step along the threshold comes near it. In baseline-noise units the six and the two have the same response rate relative to the control flies' (last row of the table above), so there the two are not further along a block at all: they have as many responses as the six and a larger effect. Read as a population of six model flies at the six's ratio of response rates and two at the two's, as the model was read as a population of wirings, the second model's pattern part hardly moves ({{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:homog_pattern ~ .3f}} for one model fly) and its loss rises ({{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:loss ~ .3f}} against {{E76/populations.csv:experiment=E76_data_side_target;readout=raw;unit=z;axis=block:homog_loss ~ .3f}}), because the six then sit at a partial block and the mean falls. The spread among the recordings is thus not a term missing from the comparison, and the two recordings' state is not one that the model reaches through a weaker APL or a lower threshold.

The family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting and the reference model's set with the same ceiling, as fitted in the firing ceiling for the KCs and fitted again from those optima against the flies in baseline-noise units, on raw spike counts. Two values without named conditions are at the trial noise matched to the control flies / to APL output blocked (TNT)

**Fitted to the effect in baseline-noise units, the best family stops short of the mean and pays on the pattern.** Against the effect in baseline-noise units the mean part of the loss, which the firing ceiling had nearly closed against the z-scored effect ([above](#firing-ceiling)), is open again: the family with the ceiling at its stronger setting is a third above the floor against the z-scored effect and at about twice the floor against this one (fourth and first rows of the table, first model column). Three fits asked how much of it the family can close. The family was fitted again from its optimum, first with only the response-rate terms of its loss against the flies' rates in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands now count them, and then with the APL-effect terms against the effect in baseline-noise units as well; the reference model's set with the same ceiling, which with its larger mean effect starts level with the family against this effect, was fitted the second way from its own optimum. The first fit hardly moves, its loss against the z-scored effect changing by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}): the change of the bands' unit left the best fit where it was. The second raises the mean effect by {{diff:E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} and lowers the loss against the effect it was fitted to by a quarter. It stops {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} short of the flies' mean, at one and a half times the floor; its pattern part rises, its ρ on the per-pair APL effect falls (second and third rows), and against the z-scored effect it is worse than before (fourth row). It makes the larger effect with more responses with APL off at the same response rate with APL on, through a higher somatic threshold ({{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the baseline's, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:thr_factor ~ .2f}}), a weaker APL→bouton scale ({{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}}) and less than half the KC–KC inhibition (a scale of {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}, from {{E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:kc_kc_inh ~ .1f}}). The reference model's set makes the same move and ends at a higher loss than the family's fit, with the lowest ρ on the per-pair APL effect of the five columns, so it does not come back as a base.

**Through the trial noise little of the gain is left.** The first two fits were put through [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise), ten pseudo-recordings of three trials, and scored on the three-trial means, as the recordings are. The noise lowers the mean APL effect of both, as it does for the fits with the ceiling made before ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and that of the fit to the effect in baseline-noise units more (seventh row). The two then differ on the loss by about what one draw of the wiring moves it (sixth row). Both are about a third short of the flies' mean effect in baseline-noise units and at more than twice the floor of the loss, where against the z-scored effect, through the same noise, they are at {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=z:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} to {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_off;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=z:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, against a floor of {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}. The pattern part through the noise is about where it is without it ({{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=noise:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} and {{E76/partF_noise.csv:model=E76-nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;level=match_on;transform=graded;distances=raw;unit=noise:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} at the noise matched to the control flies). Read as the recordings are made, fitting to the effect in baseline-noise units therefore buys little: through the noise the mean part is again the larger part of both fits' loss against that effect, as it was against the z-scored effect before the firing ceiling.

**Realism.** The three fits are inside all four realism bands, as the two they start from are (last row). The fits to the effect in baseline-noise units paid for the larger mean in breadth with APL off. At an unchanged response rate with APL on, the family has more responses with APL off, so that the ratio of the two rates moves from near the flies' toward the upper end of the flies' interval and of the band (ninth row), and more of its KCs respond to eight or more odors with APL off, where it already had more than the flies (tenth row); the reference model's set does the same. In the family the distance of the odors-per-KC distribution from the flies' with APL off grows, and in both it stays well inside its band (eleventh row). KC–KC inhibition, which no band measures, falls to less than half in both. A fit held at the flies' ratio of response rates would likely end further from the flies' mean, so the shortfall given above is the least this family leaves open. The parts on the recordings change no model, and as everywhere the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** Which unit the flies' side of the main target is held to is a choice about its mean part, like the choice of the model's readout, and it is not yet made; the mean over all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) stands in either unit. The pattern part and the order of the models on raw counts do not depend on the choice, so until it is made the families are ranked on the pattern part, and the mean part is given against both effects. If the target moves to baseline-noise units, the mean part is open again for every model, and more responses with APL off is a route that the fit has already taken, at a cost; what the flies have there and the models lack is responses that grow with a KC's breadth ([the per-KC normalization of the recordings](#per-kc-normalization)). Two later readings qualify this: weighting a fit's spike counts by the KC's breadth moves its mean effect by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at most, and the comparison of raw counts with the effect in baseline-noise units is one at the model's 0.5 s odor pulse, the same fit's mean effect on raw counts being {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} at the flies' 2 s pulse against {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)), and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=counts:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} there once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). The split of the effect by odors per KC is given in both units from here on. The state of the two strongest recordings, the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms far closer with APL output blocked (TNT), becomes a target for mechanisms that change what reaches the KCs, where the common error is largest (the fixed changes of the input screened in the next subsection, [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), do not lower the common error; they were not scored against the two recordings alone). What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The input side of the error common to all wirings: whether a change of what reaches the KCs carries it {#input-side}

**A change of what reaches the KCs does not carry the error that every wiring shares, as far as a fixed change of the input can tell. About two fifths of the common error's squared sum is of the kind that a change acting with APL on and with APL off alike reaches. On the real wiring no handle the model has on its input lowers the pattern part of the APL-effect loss by more than a small fraction of what one draw of the wiring moves it, APL inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input raises it, and every one of these changes would add to the common error if it carried over to other wirings. An input searched within a factor of two against half of the recordings holds for the other half on the real wiring and not on re-drawn wirings, and the two halves do not give the same factors. Other input for the weak odors does not help the best family.** [The glomerulus profile of APL inhibition](#glomerulus-profile) found no fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli that carries the common error, and found that the few saved models with little of it all change what reaches the KCs, each on an earlier model and with an error of its own. The input side of the error common to all wirings asked the question in the best family: whether a change of the input lowers the common error there. Everything is on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit (the first model column of the first table of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), and values are through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named. Under the readout the fit has the flies' mean effect and its loss is nearly all pattern, so the pattern part is what a change has to lower: {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse_centered ~ .3f}} on the real wiring and {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over the eight wirings, the common error, against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}. The flies' side is the mean over all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), the target that stands, with the six that are alike beside it where named ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring: as fitted, fitted again from its own parameters on two other inputs for the weak-input odors, and with each claw's input capped at 250 Hz, the setting with the lowest pattern part in the screen further down. The first five rows are through the calibrated readout; two values without named conditions are with APL on / APL off

**Other input for the weak odors does not help the best family.** The fit was made again from its own parameters on two other inputs: with [Hallem's receptor data](#hallem-input) for ms, paa, B-myr and 1-8ol, and with the input that the bounded oracle had searched for the seven weak-input odors on the reference model ([above](#gap-pairs)). With Hallem's data the loss is {{diff:E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=H;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse -- E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} higher and the mean effect short again (second model column). The error on the five pairs of ms with 2h, IaA, pa, eb and ep nearly doubles, from {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:err_ms_pairs_z8 ~ +.3f}} to {{E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=H;readout=cal:err_ms_pairs_z8 ~ +.3f}}, with Hallem's response of DL1 to ms several times the lab's. With the searched input the loss is {{diff:E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=S;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse -- E77/partA_fits.csv:fit=C2;readout=cal:apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}} above the fit's, less than one draw of the wiring moves it ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and what the input adds is a higher response rate ρ with APL on, which that search had raised through its penalty on the odors' response fractions (third model column). Neither input lowers the loss, so the weak odors' input is not where this family's error is, and the lab's input stays.

**About two fifths of the common error is within the reach of a change of the input.** A change of the input acts with APL on and with APL off alike: it moves a pair's distance in both conditions. If a model's distances with APL on follow from its distances with APL off by a relation of its own, such a change moves a pair along that relation, and the part of the error that it reaches in this way is the part that comes from where the model's distances with APL off differ from the flies'. The pattern error was therefore [split into three terms that add up to it](#fn-inherited-split): the inherited part, the error a model would have if it followed the flies' relation between the two conditions exactly, starting from its own distances with APL off; the difference between the model's relation and the flies'; and the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations, the block among them. For the mean over the eight wirings the inherited part is {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} of the common error's squared sum, and {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z6;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} against the six recordings that are alike; with the flies' relation fitted on halves of the recordings it lies between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q05:value ~ .0%}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q95:value ~ .0%}}. The departures hold {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_pair_specific ~ .0%}}, and the difference between the two relations offsets a little ({{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_curve ~ +.2f}} as a share; the three add to one). Without its inherited part the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings would be {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms_without_inherited ~ .3f}} in place of {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:pattern_rms ~ .3f}}. Most of the common error is thus in what APL does to particular pairs, which a change shared by the two conditions does not reach in this way. The split is not a bound on what a search can do on one wiring, as the last part of this subsection shows.

**Two descriptions of the common error came with the split.** Taken apart by odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), an odor's term in the common error, its share of the error on every pair it is in, follows how much more its response fraction grows in the model than in the flies when APL is removed: where the model gains more responses than the flies, its APL effect on the odor's pairs is too large. Across the 16 odors the two correlate at Pearson r {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z8:value ~ .2f}} against all eight recordings and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:per_odor_share_gain_corr_cal_z6:value ~ .2f}} against the six that are alike (the flies' responses counted by the recordings' own criterion), so this is a lead and not a result, and one that leans on the two strongest recordings. And the model's antennal lobe evens out the odors' total drive: summed over the glomeruli, the model's PN rates lie between {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:pn_sum ~ .0f}} and {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=2h:pn_sum ~ .0f}} Hz for the 16 odors, where the summed ORN responses run from {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=B-myr:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for B-myr to {{E77/pn_totals.csv:odor=1-6ol:orn_sum_pos ~ .0f}} Hz for 1-6ol.

**No handle on the input lowers the pattern part, and each would add to the common error.** Six handles that the model has on its input were screened on the fit at fixed settings: a weaker antennal-lobe normalization; other input for the weak odors with nothing fitted again; each odor's input compressed or expanded across glomeruli at an unchanged sum; a cap on each claw's input; a more equal weight for the glomeruli, by per-glomerulus drive normalization or by each glomerulus's number of claws; and bouton vesicle depletion. At every setting the somatic threshold and the APL scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, with the breadth weights computed again for the changed input. Beside them ran two [oracle](#fn-oracle) emulations that act with APL on only, the run with APL off being the fit's own: APL's weight on each bouton, or on each claw, multiplied by a power of that bouton's or claw's own input to the odor. For each setting, the change it makes to the per-pair APL effect on the real wiring was also set against the common error: the transfer is the share of the common error's squared sum that the change would remove if it were the same on every wiring.

The handles on the fit's input and the two emulations, each at its setting with the lowest pattern part: the pattern part through the calibrated readout, the APL-effect loss on raw counts, and the transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that the setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring (negative: it would add that share)
