The lowest pattern part of the screen, with each claw's input capped at 250 Hz, is {{E77/gate.csv:point_id=S4_tanh250:pattern_gain ~ .3f}} below the fit's, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}} (last column of the first table); per-glomerulus drive normalization at half strength gains as little, and every other setting of every handle raises the pattern part. The transfer is negative at every setting, {{E77/report_scalars.csv:gate_transfer_all_max:value ~ +.2f}} at best against all eight recordings and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:gate_transfer_six_max:value ~ +.2f}} against the six that are alike: what each change does on the real wiring is not what the wirings share, and carried over to them it would add to the common error. A weaker antennal-lobe normalization does raise the mean APL effect on raw counts, from {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} at the third of its four steps, where the loss on raw counts is {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:raw_loss ~ .3f}} against the fit's {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, and it pays with the pattern part ({{E77/screen.csv:point_id=S1_inhadd1000:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} against {{E77/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}}). The two emulations raise the pattern part, and the loss on raw counts with it. Nothing came near what had been set beforehand for going on to fits on several wirings, so no handle was fitted.

**A searched input holds over recordings on its own wiring, and not over wirings.** With no handle to fit, the input itself was searched, as the bounded oracle had searched it for the weak odors ([above](#gap-pairs)). On the fit at its fitted parameters on the real wiring, the ORN response of each of eb, 1-8ol, IaA, ep, 2h, 1-6ol, pa, 6al, 1-5ol and ms, one odor after the other, was multiplied in every glomerulus by a factor between one half and two, searched for the lowest pattern part against one half of the recordings, with a penalty once the odor's response fraction left ±15 % of the fit's. The recordings were split by fly, the two strongest recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) in different halves, and the search was run once against each half. It is an [oracle](#fn-oracle): what a corrected input could at most buy, not a measurement. Each searched input was then scored against the half it had not seen, with both response rates set again, on the real wiring and on three re-drawn wirings of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population) at their own fits, and as the mean over the four.

The pattern part of the APL-effect loss through the calibrated readout against the half of the recordings that the search did not see (lower is better), with the lab's input and with the searched input, and the gain (the first minus the second). | mean over the four wirings | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}} | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} | {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=pop4;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}} |

The search has the freedom to fit: against the half it was run on, the pattern part on the real wiring falls from {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} and from {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=lab;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}} to {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=real;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_rms ~ .3f}}. On the real wiring part of that holds for the half it never saw, in both directions and by about what one draw of the wiring moves the loss (first row). On the three re-drawn wirings it does not, the gains there lying between {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfA;wiring=P2;readout=cal;target=halfB:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}} and {{E77/oracle_scores.csv:input=oracle_halfB;wiring=P1;readout=cal;target=halfA:pattern_gain_vs_lab ~ +.3f}}, and the mean over the four wirings, the kind of mean in which the common error is defined, gains next to nothing (last row). The factors themselves do not repeat: for each of the ten odors, the correlation over the 36 glomeruli between the factors found against the two halves, on a log scale, lies between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_min:value ~ .2f}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_max:value ~ .2f}}, with a median of {{E77/report_scalars.csv:halves_factor_corr_median:value ~ .2f}}. A search free to set every glomerulus of every odor thus finds something that holds over recordings on the wiring it was run on, that wiring's own remainder, and nothing that the wirings share.

**Realism.** Every model of this subsection has the control flies' response rate with APL on, fitted or held, and the four columns of the first table are inside all four realism bands, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10 (lower rows). So are both searched inputs on each of the four wirings. Every setting of the screen is inside the four bands as they count now; counted by the recordings' own criterion, the two compressive exponents on the input, the lowest cap, the stronger of the two bouton emulations and the stronger depletion leave a band on the number of odors per KC, and no reading above rests on them. The searched inputs are oracle inputs, each glomerulus's response between half and twice the recorded one and many of them at those bounds, which no measurement supports and on which the two halves of the recordings do not agree. What the bands do not see is the fit's own and unchanged: the release through the many-claw KCs when APL is removed, a somatic threshold under half the baseline's and an APL→bouton scale near its bound ([above](#wiring-population)). Nothing here was bought with realism, because nothing was gained beyond one wiring. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), and Hallem's values are at ten times the concentration of the KC recordings for ms, paa and 1-8ol.

**What follows.** No draw of the wiring carries the common error, no amount of inhibition per odor ([above](#apl-effect-parts)), no fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli of the kind tried ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and now no fixed change of the input and no APL inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input. In this family the common error is therefore not on the input side, as far as these handles and a search within a factor of two go, and it stays unexplained by the mechanisms the family has. Most of it lies in the two sides' pair-by-pair departures from their own relations between the conditions, which a change acting through the distances that the conditions share does not reach. Of the changes to what reaches the KCs, one was not among the handles, a per-claw knee near the largest PN rate; it has been run since and does not carry the common error either ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)). What else is left lies outside what was screened: how APL's inhibition unfolds in time, differences between types of KCs, and inhibition that depends on the odor in another form (one such form, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share, has since been tested as a proxy on the input and does not carry the common error: [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps), the next subsection; the length of the odor pulse, the types of KCs and changes that a long block could have left in the KCs have been run as well, and none carries it: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)). The two descriptions above go with them as leads, each odor's growth in responses when APL is removed and the evening-out of the odors' total drive in the model's antennal lobe, with the caution that weakening that normalization alone cost the pattern part. If the input is taken up again, it is as a change fitted on several wirings at once, tested by whether two halves of the recordings give the same factors. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The APL calyx maps against the connectome: what APL's own activity in the calyx looks like, and whether glomeruli that share calyx space carry the error common to the wirings {#apl-calyx-maps}

**APL's activity in the calyx, imaged for three odors, is reliable and for the most part one pattern that all odors share. The part that is an odor's own is smaller, repeats between presentations and varies over several micrometres, and pa's response lies lower in the image than ms's at equal strength. Maps predicted from where the PN boutons lie in seven connectome calyces match the measured differences between odors no better than the same boutons with their glomerulus labels permuted, with the orientation and the depth of the images unknown, and the maps of the model with local APL units are flatter and less alike between odors than the flies' at every coupling. The glomeruli that the esters share do lie closer together in the calyx than random sets, but inhibition that follows each glomerulus's neighbourhood there, in place of the calyx as a whole, removes too little of the common error on odors left out of its fit. A spatially local APL at the boutons was therefore not fitted.** [The input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) left the common error unexplained by the mechanisms that the best family has, and all of them treat APL as one cell that inhibits the whole calyx alike. An APL that acts locally would be a mechanism of another kind: glomeruli whose PN boutons lie in the same part of the calyx would be inhibited together, and of the six odors among which the model's APL effect is too small, the five esters (2h, IaA, pa, eb and ep) have strongly driven glomeruli in common. Local APL units had been tried early, on a model without the later mechanisms, and had left the KCs' odor-odor distances where a single APL puts them (among what did not matter, further up), with nothing measured to say how local APL is. The APL calyx maps against the connectome took that measurement from Yang's calcium imaging of APL itself and asked two things of it without fitting a model, both fixed beforehand: whether maps of APL's activity predicted from the wiring match the measured ones, and whether the nearness of glomeruli in the calyx predicts the common error on odors it was not fitted to, by removing 15 % or more of its squared sum and more than permuted glomerulus labels remove. Only with both was a spatially local APL to be fitted in the best family.

**The maps.** The recordings are of APL in a single plane through the calyx, {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings from {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies. Each holds pa, paa and ms as concentration series (pa from 10^-6.8 to 10^-4.4, paa from 10^-6.3 to 10^-3.0, ms from 10^-7.7 to 10^-2), every stimulus given twice, and one map per presentation: the change in fluorescence over its baseline around the peak of the response, inside an outline of the calyx drawn for the recording. The files do not say how the images are oriented, at what depth the plane lies or how large a pixel is. Positions are therefore given along the image's own axes, and lengths in pixels, with micrometres at an assumed 0.3 µm per pixel (the size of the hemibrain calyx against the outlines implies slightly less, if the plane cuts the calyx near its widest).

**One pattern shared by all odors, and a smaller part that is each odor's own.** The maps are reliable: the two presentations of a stimulus correlate, pixel by pixel inside the outline, at Pearson r {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} (the median over recordings at each odor's highest concentration; {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=all_pfo:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} and {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=first_in_block:repeat_r_top_median ~ .2f}} with two other ways of taking the baseline from the solvent presentations). Maps of different odors are almost as alike, at {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:different_odor_r_top_median ~ .2f}}, though not in every fly: in {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings_ms_vs_pa_top_below_0p8 ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_baseline_summary.csv:baseline=order_matched:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings the maps of ms and pa correlate below 0.8. Most of a recording is one spatial pattern common to all its stimuli. The first singular vector of its matrix of stimuli by pixels holds {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} of the summed squares at the finest smoothing (2 pixels) and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means kept;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} at the coarsest (20 pixels), and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} and {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=20.0;mode=means removed;column=share_first_sv:measured_all_median ~ .0%}} when each map's mean is removed first, so that shapes alone are compared (medians over recordings; left column of the figure). What is left of a map without that pattern, the remainder (the residual of the figure), is what is specific to a stimulus, and it is not noise. It repeats between the two presentations at every smoothing (second column), and the remainders of the two presentations stay correlated over {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median_px ~ .0f}} pixels, {{E79/E79_model_vs_measured.csv:blur_px=2.0;mode=means kept;column=resid_crossrep_len:measured_all_median ~ .1f}} µm at the assumed pixel size (right column): an odor's own part of APL's activity varies over several micrometres, a small fraction of the calyx.

![The shared and the odor-specific parts of the APL calyx maps against the width of the smoothing (Gaussian, in pixels), for each recording (grey) and as the median over recordings (black); top row with each map's mean kept, bottom row with it removed. From left to right: the share of the summed squares of a recording's stimulus × pixel matrix that its first singular vector holds, the pattern common to all stimuli; the correlation of the residual, a map without that pattern, between the two presentations of a stimulus; the correlation between the residuals of different odors, which the construction pulls below zero, since the residuals sum to zero, so that it decides nothing; and the distance over which the residuals of the two presentations stay correlated (to 1/e), with the same for smoothed white noise (dotted). The residual statistics are over each odor's two highest concentrations.](results/E79_apl_calyx_constraints/E79_shared_specific.png)

**Where pa's response lies against ms's.** Within an odor, a stronger response lies higher in the image, in every fly: the centroid of the response along the vertical axis of the image moves down with the logarithm of the response's strength in {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=slope_per_log_mean:n_flies_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=slope_per_log_mean:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies. Two odors can therefore only be compared at equal strength. At matched strength, for each recording the two concentrations at which the odors' mean responses over the calyx are closest, the centroid of pa's response lies lower in the image than that of ms's by {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:mean_shift ~ .3f}} of the outline's height (mean over flies, a fly's hemispheres averaged; 90 % interval over resampled flies {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:lo90 ~ .3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:hi90 ~ .3f}}; lower in {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies_positive ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=pa - ms;axis=y:n_flies ~ .0f}} flies), and by {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:mean ~ .3f}} ({{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:lo90 ~ .3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_adjusted.csv:axis=y;quantity=offset_pa_minus_ms:hi90 ~ .3f}}) when the offset between the odors is fitted at equal strength over all concentrations. For paa the shift is about half as large, {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:mean_shift ~ .3f}}, and its interval includes zero ({{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:lo90 ~ +.3f}} to {{E79/E79_profile_centroid_shift.csv:pair=paa - ms;axis=y:hi90 ~ +.3f}}). The shift of pa is small against the calyx and present in most flies. Which anatomical direction it is cannot be said without the orientation of the images.

![The response along the two axes of the image, in ten bins over the bounding box of the calyx outline: the share of pa's response in each bin minus that of ms's (top) and paa's minus ms's (bottom) at matched strength, along the vertical axis from top to bottom (left) and along the horizontal axis with left hemispheres mirrored (right). Grey: single flies; black with band: the mean over flies and its 90 % interval. Dashed: the same difference in the maps of the model with local APL units at three couplings, drawn as if the top of the image were dorsal.](results/E79_apl_calyx_constraints/E79_profiles.png)

**The model with local APL units does not make such maps.** That model divides APL into compartments defined from the connectome, each with a potential of its own, coupled with a strength that was never set from data. Its saved potentials (an early model at the conventional 5 %, at three couplings) were placed on APL's neurites in the hemibrain calyx, projected as the calyx is seen from posterior, and given the statistics of the measured maps.

Both are smoothed over 2 pixels, 0.6 µm at the assumed pixel size, and the model's maps are of the whole depth of the calyx

At every coupling the model's maps are less alike between odors than the flies' and far more even over the calyx (first and third rows): in the flies the odors share most of a map that varies strongly from place to place, and in the model each odor has a weak pattern of its own on a nearly even ground. Coupling the units evens the maps out further without making them more alike, and only the distance over which an odor's own part varies is near the measured one. Part of the flies' shared pattern may be anatomy, the density of APL's neurites in the imaged plane, which unit potentials do not have, and pa was imaged more than one log unit below the model's pa. If local units are taken up again, how uneven a map is and how alike two odors' maps are is what their coupling would be set by.

**The wiring does not predict the odor-specific part, as far as the images allow the test.** If APL's activity at a place follows the PN input there, a map can be predicted from a connectome: every PN bouton of the calyx at its position, weighted by its number of release sites and by the model's PN rate for the odor in the bouton's glomerulus ([how the maps were predicted and scored](#fn-calyx-maps)). The rates are those of the PN stage of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit. The positions are those of seven calyces from four connectome data sets (the right calyx of the hemibrain and both calyces of FlyWire, of the male CNS and of BANC) and of the model's own set of hemibrain boutons. Because the orientation and the depth of the images are unknown, each prediction was made for slabs at every depth and for the whole calyx, at three smoothings, and set against each recording's map in four orientations, and the best correlation was kept. The test is on the differences between odors, pa minus ms and paa minus ms at matched strength, each map divided by its mean. Its null is the same procedure with the glomerulus labels of the PN rates permuted, 1,000 times, which keeps the anatomy and the freedom to choose orientation, depth and smoothing.

For pa minus ms no calyx's prediction reaches the 95th percentile of its permutations. For paa minus ms one of the eight does, barely, the right calyx of BANC, which is about what sixteen comparisons give by chance. The correlations themselves are not low, but permuted labels reach them as easily, since orientation, depth and smoothing are chosen for the permutations too. Predictions driven by the positions of the claws, or by those of the KCs' synapses onto APL with the fit's spike counts, do no better. For the map of a single odor the anatomy alone, the density of the synapses between PNs and APL with no odor in it, matches as well as the odor-weighted prediction: on the hemibrain calyx {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=anatomy;comparison=pa;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} against {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=bouton;comparison=pa;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} for pa, {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=anatomy;comparison=paa;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} against {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=bouton;comparison=paa;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} for paa and {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=anatomy;comparison=ms;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} against {{E79/connectome_map_pooled.csv:calyx=hemibrain_R;alternative=bouton;comparison=ms;flip=best:mean_best_r ~ .2f}} for ms, and over the calyces neither is consistently ahead. The measured differences are not what fails: in most recordings they repeat between the two presentations.

One lead is left, for the orientation. For pa minus ms, with the seven calyces pooled, the same orientation is the best one in {{E79/connectome_map_flip_consensus.csv:alternative=bouton;comparison=pa-ms:n_recordings_won ~ .0f}} of the {{E79/connectome_map_flip_consensus.csv:alternative=bouton;comparison=pa-ms:n_recordings ~ .0f}} recordings, the image turned by 180 degrees, which is more often than in {{E79/connectome_map_flip_consensus.csv:alternative=bouton;comparison=pa-ms:null_pct_n_won ~ .0f}} % of the permutations, while the correlation at that orientation is higher than in {{E79/connectome_map_flip_consensus.csv:alternative=bouton;comparison=pa-ms:null_pct_mean_r ~ .0f}} % of them, inside the null. Turned that way, pa's response, lower in the image than ms's, would be the more dorsal one, as most of the calyces predict. Several such comparisons were made, and paa minus ms prefers no orientation, so this is a lead and not a result.

The test is weaker than it can be made. Scoring every orientation and depth gives the permutations the same room. Every pa map was imaged more than one log unit below the pa of the model's input (10^-4.4 and lower against 10^-3), outside the one log unit within which data at another concentration stand in on this page ([footnote](#fn-concentrations)); the paa and ms maps are within it at some of their concentrations only, and paa's PN rates come from ORN data at 10^-4, the substitute used throughout. And the pattern that all odors share may be the density of APL's neurites more than its activity. The maps thus neither support a map of APL's activity made from the wiring nor rule one out: that test waits for the orientation, the depth and the pixel size of the images.

**Glomeruli that share calyx space, and the common error.** The second question does not need the maps. The co-localization of two glomeruli is how close their boutons lie: the mean, over pairs of boutons with one from each glomerulus, weighted by the boutons' numbers of release sites, of a Gaussian function of the distance between them, with a width of 2, 4, 8 or 16 µm. It was computed for the glomeruli with ORN input in each of the eight calyces, and as the mean over the seven connectome calyces, their consensus. It is a property of the anatomy on which the connectomes agree once the width is 4 µm or more: over the pairs of glomeruli, the two least alike calyces correlate at Pearson r {{E79/coloc_agreement.csv:lambda_um=2.0;calyx_a=malecns_R;calyx_b=model_hemibrain_R:pearson_r ~ .2f}} at 2 µm, {{E79/coloc_agreement.csv:lambda_um=4.0;calyx_a=flywire_L;calyx_b=model_hemibrain_R:pearson_r ~ .2f}} at 4 µm and {{E79/coloc_agreement.csv:lambda_um=8.0;calyx_a=flywire_L;calyx_b=model_hemibrain_R:pearson_r ~ .2f}} at 8 µm.

How close the glomeruli of a set lie to each other in the calyx: the percentile of the set's mean co-localization among 10,000 random sets of as many glomeruli, in the consensus of the connectome calyces (50: as close as a random set; near 100: closer than nearly all)

| | width of the neighbourhood {span=4} |
| glomerulus set | 2 µm | 4 µm | 8 µm | 16 µm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| four glomeruli driven by the esters, named beforehand as those they share: DM1, DM2, DM3, VM2 | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=2.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=4.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=8.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=16.0:pct ~ .1f}} |
| the four glomeruli most over-represented among the claws of the fit's KCs that respond to two or more of 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms: DM2, DM3, DM5, DM6 | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=c2_coresponders;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=2.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=c2_coresponders;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=4.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=c2_coresponders;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=8.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=c2_coresponders;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=16.0:pct ~ .1f}} |
| the eight oracle glomeruli | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=oracle_eight;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=2.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=oracle_eight;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=4.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=oracle_eight;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=8.0:pct ~ .1f}} | {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=oracle_eight;calyx=consensus;lambda_um=16.0:pct ~ .1f}} |

The premise of a local APL holds for the esters. The four glomeruli named beforehand as those they share lie closer to each other than nearly all random sets of four at every width up to 8 µm (first row), and do so in each calyx taken by itself: at 4 µm between percentile {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=malecns_L;lambda_um=4.0:pct ~ .1f}} and percentile {{E79/coloc_sets.csv:set=ester_shared;calyx=flywire_R;lambda_um=4.0:pct ~ .1f}} over the eight. The four glomeruli that the fit's KCs responding to several of those odors draw on most ([above](#glomerulus-profile)) are nearly as close at the two smallest widths and not beyond, and the eight oracle glomeruli are no closer than random sets.

Whether that nearness can carry the common error was asked with a proxy on the model's PN rates, without simulation ([how it was scored](#fn-calyx-maps)): the change in the cosine distance between two odors' PN rates when each glomerulus is inhibited in proportion to the activity near its own boutons, the rates of all glomeruli weighted by their co-localization with it, instead of in proportion to the odor's mean rate, as an APL that acts on the whole calyx would inhibit it. It was computed for the 120 pairs with subtractive and with divisive inhibition, at two strengths each and at the four widths, on the eight calyces and the consensus, 144 settings in all. For each setting the change was scaled to the common error on the pairs of 15 odors and scored on the 15 pairs of the odor left out, over the 16 odors, and the same was done with the glomeruli permuted in the co-localization matrix.

In most settings the change goes the way that would correct the error, and weakly. The best setting (the right calyx of the male CNS, 2 µm, subtractive) correlates with the common error at Pearson r {{E79/coloc_proxy.csv:calyx=malecns_R;lambda_um=2.0;form=sub;strength=0.5:corr_with_common_error ~ .2f}} over the 120 pairs (figure; negative is the correcting direction, a pair moving apart where the model's APL effect is too small), and removes {{E79/coloc_proxy.csv:calyx=malecns_R;lambda_um=2.0;form=sub;strength=0.5:in_sample_share ~ .1%}} of the common error's squared sum on the pairs it was scaled to and {{E79/coloc_proxy.csv:calyx=malecns_R;lambda_um=2.0;form=sub;strength=0.5:loo_share ~ .1%}} on left-out odors, where 15 % was asked. Among its own permutations that lies at percentile {{E79/coloc_proxy.csv:calyx=malecns_R;lambda_um=2.0;form=sub;strength=0.5:loo_null_pct ~ .1f}}, and among the best settings of permuted matrices, the comparison that is fair to the best of 144, at percentile {{E79/coloc_proxy.csv:calyx=malecns_R;lambda_um=2.0;form=sub;strength=0.5:loo_null_pct_of_best ~ .1f}}. None of the 144 settings passes.

![The best of the 144 settings of the co-localization proxy (the right calyx of the male CNS, a neighbourhood of 2 µm, subtractive inhibition). For each of the 120 odor pairs: the change in the cosine distance between the two odors' PN rates when each glomerulus's inhibition follows the activity near its boutons instead of the mean over the glomeruli (horizontal, mean removed), against the error common to all wirings (vertical; negative where the model's APL effect is too small). A change that corrected the error would be positive where the error is negative.](results/E79_apl_calyx_constraints/E79_coloc_proxy.png)

The premise is right and the consequence too small: the esters' glomeruli share calyx space, and inhibition that follows that space moves the pairs' input distances the right way, by too little and not dependably on odors it was not scaled to. A spatially local APL at the boutons was therefore not fitted in the best family. The proxy is static, PN rates under one rule of inhibition, and a local APL inside the network could act differently; the test was there to decide whether that fit is worth making, and at neighbourhoods of 2 to 16 µm it says that it is not.

**Realism.** No model was changed or fitted here, so the realism bands do not apply: the only model quantities used are the PN rates of the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, which the bands do not score, and the saved potentials of the early model with local APL units, which is not a candidate base.

**What follows.** An APL that acts locally at the boutons, along the calyx space that glomeruli share, is left without support as the source of the common error at the widths tested, beside the fixed profile over the glomeruli ([above](#glomerulus-profile)) and the inhibition that grows with a bouton's or a claw's own input ([above](#input-side)). It is not excluded, since the test was a proxy on the input and the maps could not be oriented. What would reopen it lies with the data: the orientation, the depth and the pixel size of the images, with which the prediction from the wiring is tested at one orientation and one depth, the fair test of whether the wiring predicts APL's map; and, since the common error sets 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms against 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, APL maps of eb or 2h against 1-6ol or 1-8ol at the 10^-3 of the KC recordings, which would show what the three odors imaged cannot, whether APL's activity differs in place between the two groups. If the prediction then matches the maps and the co-localization at the matched depth passes the test above, the local fit is taken up. What remained for the common error on the model's side outside the calyx is in the next subsection ([the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); what is still open is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error: what the length of the odor pulse does to the model's match, and whether anything left on the model's side carries the error common to the wirings {#remaining-candidates}

**The length of the odor pulse does not change the model's match to the main target under the calibrated readout, and it does on raw spike counts. With the flies' 2 s pulse in place of the model's 0.5 s, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit keeps its loss under the readout, while on raw counts its mean APL effect halves and its loss rises by more than half, because the model's APL nearly silences the response after the first half second; with a firing ceiling, where raw counts and the readout give one number, that number rises as well, by a fifth. The raw-count numbers of the main target are therefore tied to the model's 0.5 s pulse at the settings of these fits; the flies' recording protocol in the model, the next subsection but one, lifts this for the family with the firing ceiling once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor. None of the candidates left on the model's side lowers the error common to all wirings, and every one would add to it: types of KCs, changes that act only with APL off, how many KCs each odor recruits, and an input shared by all glomeruli. A threshold that is lower with APL on than with APL off lowers the mean APL effect, and response amplitudes that grow with a KC's breadth do not raise it toward the flies' mean in baseline-noise units.** [The input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side) had closed fixed changes of what reaches the KCs and named what was left on the model's side: how the response unfolds in time, types of KCs, inhibition that depends on the odor in another form, and how much each odor's response fraction grows when APL is removed. This experiment took what neither [the APL calyx maps against the connectome](#apl-calyx-maps) nor the per-claw knee ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee), the next subsection) covers, on the real wiring and with nothing fitted again: on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and, where named, on the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting (the second model column of the second table of [the data side of the main target](#data-side)).

**The pulse.** The flies were given a 2 s odor pulse, and a response in the recordings is the mean of a KC's signal from 2 to 8 s after the pulse's onset ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)). The model's odor has always lasted 0.5 s, with spikes counted until 0.25 s after it ends. Both fits were run with pulses of 1 s and 2 s, spikes again counted until 0.25 s after the pulse, with both response rates held at the fit's own, which changes little (at 2 s the breadth-2 fit needs a somatic threshold {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:thr_factor ~ .2f}} times and an APL scale {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:apl_factor ~ .2f}} times the fitted ones).

**Under the readout the pulse does not matter; on raw counts it does.** Through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) the breadth-2 fit's loss at the flies' pulse is within {{diff:E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:cal_loss -- E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse0.5_fixed:cal_loss ~ .3f}} of its loss at 0.5 s, less than one draw of the wiring moves it ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}), with the mean effect still near the flies' and the pattern part where it was (first three rows, second values). On raw counts the mean effect falls with each lengthening of the pulse, to half at 2 s, and the loss rises by more than half (first values). A longer pulse had been expected to raise the mean effect on raw counts; it lowers it because of when the model's KCs fire. With APL on nearly all spikes of the 2 s pulse fall in its first 0.5 s, and with APL off a third come later (sixth row): the model's APL all but silences the response that outlasts the onset. The late spikes with APL off come from few KCs, with patterns further apart between odors than the onset's (a mean distance of {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the second half second against {{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0-0.5:mean_dist_off ~ .2f}} in the first). They raise the distances with APL off toward those with APL on, which hardly move (fifth row), so the effect shrinks; the readout's saturation removes most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, which is why its numbers hold. In the family with the firing ceiling the adaptation cuts the late spikes with APL off as well, and the mean effect falls less; but there the readout has nothing left to compress, so the one number that both definitions give rises with the pulse, to about the breadth-2 fit's loss under the readout (last two columns). All of this is at parameters fitted with the 0.5 s pulse: what shapes a sustained response in the model (the adaptation of the PNs, KC–KC inhibition, APL) had not been fitted at 2 s (both families have been since: [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), and with APL on the response after the first half second is too sparse for a per-pair APL effect of its own ({{E80/pulse_windows.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;window=0.5-1:n_pairs_defined ~ .0f}} of the 120 pairs are defined in the second half second).

**No candidate lowers the pattern part, and each would add to the common error.** Under the readout the breadth-2 fit has the flies' mean effect, so the pattern part is what a candidate has to lower: {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} on the real wiring and {{E72/population.csv:group=all:cal_pattern ~ .3f}} for the mean over the eight wirings, the common error, against a floor of {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_rmse_centered:mean ~ .3f}}. Four candidates were run on the fit at fixed settings, with both response rates held at the fit's own where the candidate does not set them, and put to the test of [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side): an input shared by all glomeruli, as lateral excitation in the antennal lobe would add; each odor's response rates put on the flies' by a threshold per odor, an [oracle](#fn-oracle) for how many KCs each odor recruits; changes that act only with APL off, as a block of APL output lasting three days could have left them in the KCs (each KC's threshold raised with the KC's own activity, or the threshold of one type of KC raised); and APL's weight on one type of KC halved or doubled. A fifth was read as a curve and not put to the test: a threshold that is lower with APL on than with APL off, the other form that an adaptation to the block could take, with APL made stronger until the response rate with APL on is the fit's.

The candidates on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit, each at its setting with the lowest pattern part: the pattern part through the calibrated readout, the mean APL effect and the APL-effect loss on raw counts, and the transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that the setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring (negative: it would add that share)

The lowest pattern part of the screen is {{E80/gate.csv:point_id=B4_beta0.25:pattern_gain ~ .3f}} below the fit's, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}. It comes from the mildest threshold raised with a KC's activity, which gives up three quarters of the mean effect on raw counts, and every steeper step raises the pattern part. The transfer is negative at every setting of every candidate, against all eight recordings and against the six that are alike: what each does on the real wiring is not what the wirings share, and carried over to them it would add to the common error. With each odor's response rates on the flies', the per-odor part of the pattern error stays between {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B3_throff_z:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}} and {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B3_thr_z:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}} (the fit's {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=base:cal_per_odor ~ .3f}}; floor {{E66/data_floor_parts.csv:data=graded;stat=apl_effect_per_odor:mean ~ .3f}}), so how many KCs each odor recruits when APL is removed, a lead of the input side, is no lever in this family. Nor does a type of KC stand out: read from the saved fits with the KCs of one type alone, the pattern part of the mean over the eight wirings is {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=a'b':pattern ~ .3f}} for the α′/β′ KCs, {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=ab:pattern ~ .3f}} for the α/β KCs and {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=g:pattern ~ .3f}} for the γ KCs, against {{E80/type_split.csv:kc_type=all:pattern ~ .3f}} with all of them, and the error among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al keeps its sign and most of its size in each. Nothing came near what had been set for going on to fits on several wirings, so no candidate was fitted.

**A threshold lower with APL on lowers the mean effect.** Had the KCs raised their thresholds during the block, the control flies' KCs would have the lower ones, and a model with a lower threshold and a stronger APL in its APL-on condition was expected to have the larger mean effect. It has a smaller one. With each KC's threshold with APL on divided by 1.1, 1.25, 1.5 or 2, the mean APL effect on raw counts falls at every step, from {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_identity:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} in the breadth-2 fit and from {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_identity:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_c2:raw_mean ~ +.3f}} in the family with the firing ceiling, where the flies' is {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in the recordings' z-scored units and {{data:noise_apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}} in baseline-noise units. The pattern part is above the fit's at every step (last row of the table for the mildest), and holding the response rate with APL on takes an APL {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c1.1:apl_factor ~ .1f}} to {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:apl_factor ~ .1f}} times as strong.

**Amplitudes that grow with a KC's breadth do not raise the mean.** In baseline-noise units no fit has the flies' mean effect, and what the flies have there and the models lack is responses that grow with the number of odors a KC responds to ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). Read from the recordings and the saved fits, without simulation, the family with the firing ceiling already has the summed squared response where the flies have it: with APL off its KCs at eight or more odors hold {{E80/amplitude_by_breadth.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;condition=APL off;cls=8+:share_sq ~ .0%}} of it, against {{E80/amplitude_by_breadth.csv:source=APL output blocked (TNT);cls=8+:share_sq ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT). Weighting the fit's counts by the number of odors a KC responds to, raised to a power between 0.1 and 0.5, moves its mean effect on raw counts by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at the most, at the power that the control flies' amplitudes give ({{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:p ~ .2f}}), where {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ .3f}} is missing, and it raises the pattern part against the effect in those units (from {{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:pattern ~ .3f}} to {{E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:pattern ~ .3f}}). The shortfall of the mean in baseline-noise units is not in how amplitudes grow with breadth.

**Realism.** With the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands count now, every setting put to the test is inside all four bands, and so are the fits at the longer pulses, whose response rates and odors per KC the pulse hardly moves (lower rows of the first table). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as until 2026-11-10, the two largest shared inputs (the one of the table among them), the steepest threshold raised with activity, the larger step on the thresholds of the α/β and of the α′/β′ KCs, the permuted control and the control in the opposite direction leave the band on the number of odors per KC with APL off; none is near passing, and no reading above rests on them. Of the threshold lower with APL on, the divisors of 1.5 and 2 on the breadth-2 fit and of 1.5 on the family with the ceiling leave the band on the response rate ρ with APL on as it counts now ({{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c1.5:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_c2:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}} and {{E80/b1_curve.csv:point_id=B1_fit0_c1.5:rate_rho_on ~ .2f}}, where 0.37 or more is asked), and by the recordings' own criterion two more of its settings, on the family with the ceiling, leave a band. What the bands do not see is hard to defend at the 2 s pulse: the hardest-driven KC of the breadth-2 fit fires {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:max_count_on ~ .0f}} spikes to one odor with APL on and {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off, where the family with the ceiling stays at {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E80/pulse.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held:max_count_off ~ .0f}}. So are the stronger APL that the threshold lower with APL on needs, and the common threshold of {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B4_beta0.5:thr_factor ~ .2f}} down to {{E80/screen.csv:point_id=B4_beta2:thr_factor ~ .2f}} of the fitted one that meets the steeper thresholds raised with activity. Nothing was gained here, so nothing was bought with realism. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The candidates that the input side had left open on the model's side are closed for this family, as far as a screen at fixed settings on one wiring closes them, and on that side the common error was left to how a claw passes its input on, the per-claw knee, which has been run since and does not carry it either ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee), the next subsection). The result that reaches beyond this subsection is the pulse. Every raw-count number of the main target on this page sets the model's response to a 0.5 s pulse against the flies' mean over 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s pulse, and, at the settings of the fits made so far, holds for the 0.5 s pulse only: the mean APL effect on raw counts, the level that the firing ceiling reaches on raw counts ([above](#firing-ceiling)) and the comparison of raw counts with the flies' effect in baseline-noise units ([above](#data-side)) among them. The readout's numbers hold at either pulse in the family without a ceiling. It had been set before the run that a worse match would mean repeating the main numbers at the flies' pulse before anything else. The match got worse on raw counts and not under the readout, and the repeat has been made ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol), the next subsection but one): read as the flies were recorded, the family with the firing ceiling has its raw-count numbers back once the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor, and the family without a ceiling does not, after a fit at 2 s either, so that for it the calibrated readout stays the reading that does not depend on the pulse. What remains for the target itself is on the data's side and waits on the experimenter: which recordings make the target, and when in the response the flies' APL effect is made, which means over one window cannot show. Both are with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The high per-claw knee without a dead zone: whether selecting responders at the claw holds apart the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input {#claw-knee}

**A per-claw knee near the largest PN rate holds the odor pairs with near-identical ORN input apart, as the flies' KCs do, only when a claw passes nothing below it. That hard knee leaves ms and B-myr without responses and about doubles the pattern part of the APL-effect loss. As soon as a claw passes a tenth of its input below the knee, the gain on those pairs is gone, and a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input does not reach them either. The per-claw transfer is therefore closed for the best family on the main target. What the hard knee does bring toward the flies is which KCs are released when APL is removed.** Six of the 120 odor pairs have nearly the same ORN input, a distance between the two odors' ORN responses below 0.25: eb with ep, 6al with t2h, IaA with pa, 2h with pa, 1-5ol with 1-6ol and 2h with IaA, none of them with an odor at a substituted ORN concentration. The flies' KCs hold these pairs apart, and more so with APL than without. The breadth-2 APL-effect fit separates them less in both conditions and has about half the flies' APL effect on them, the mean of the per-pair APL effect over the six (the KC data and the first model column of the table below). Four of the six are among the esters, where the common error has the model's APL effect too small. On the bouton model without the later mechanisms, what holds these pairs apart is a per-claw knee near the top of the PN rates, which in the model reach {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:top_pn_rate ~ .0f}} Hz: a knee at 130 Hz with nothing passed below it takes the six pairs' APL effect on raw counts from {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:base_raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr130:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, where knees at 40 to 100 Hz leave it between {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr100:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/archive_knee_variants.csv:bouton_thr70:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, and it leaves 1-8ol, ms and B-myr without a responding KC. With such a knee the somatic threshold falls and a KC responds through the one or two claws that sit on an odor's strongest boutons: the responders are selected at the claw and no longer at the soma. The high per-claw knee without a dead zone asked whether that selection holds the six pairs apart in the best family without silencing the weak odors, once the knee has no dead zone, the range of input below it that counts for nothing: a claw then passes a fraction of its input below the knee (the reduced slope that had been tried below the 70 Hz threshold of the early models, further up). The other form tried is a knee set relative to each odor's strongest input.

Everything is on the breadth-2 APL-effect fit on the real wiring (the first model column of the first table of [the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings](#wiring-population)), scored against all eight recordings with APL output blocked (TNT), through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout) unless raw counts are named. The knee was put into the fit at fixed scales: at 70, 100, 115 and 130 Hz, with nothing passed below it (a hard knee) or with a tenth, a quarter or half of a claw's input passed below it; softened over 15 Hz at the two settings nearest the fit; and at 0.5, 0.7 and 0.85 of the odor's largest bouton rate, that level taken off every bouton's output with APL on and with APL off. At each setting the somatic threshold and the APL→KC scale were set again until the numbers of responses with APL off and with APL on were the fit's, with the breadth weights computed again for the changed transfer. The KC–KC scale was lowered in proportion to the somatic threshold, because a knee cuts the drive to the soma several-fold and lateral inhibition, which is driven by the other KCs' spikes, does not shrink with it. Hard knees at 100 and 130 Hz were also fitted, from the fit's parameters and with its loss. What a setting had to do before fits on re-drawn wirings would follow had been set beforehand: reduce the ester group's error by a third (the mean error of the model's per-pair APL effect over the 15 pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms, where the common error has the effect too small; the alcohol group's error is the same over the 6 pairs among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al, where it is too large) and raise the six pairs' APL effect by 0.03, at a loss of {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:loss_limit ~ .3f}} or less, with every odor keeping at least half of its response fraction.

**The hard knee holds the pairs apart, and pays with the weak odors and the pattern.** With nothing passed below 130 Hz the six pairs' APL effect on raw counts rises from the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} at fixed scales and to {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} fitted, against the flies' {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:data_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, mostly through their distance with APL on. The same knee turns the ester group's error from too little effect into too much, doubles the alcohol group's, leaves ms and B-myr without a responding KC in either condition and about doubles the pattern part of the loss. ρ on the per-pair APL effect falls to about half, and the mean APL effect, which the fit has at the flies' under the readout, falls by a third (third and last model columns). At 115 Hz the hard knee takes the ester group's error to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:cal_err_ester ~ +.3f}} and raises the six pairs' effect by {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:six_raise ~ +.3f}} only, at a loss of {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0:cal_loss ~ .3f}}; at 100 Hz, at fixed scales or fitted, it does not raise them at all (fitted: fifth model column). This is what the hard knee did on the early bouton model, and breadth-weighted APL and KC–KC inhibition change nothing in it: in this family the ester group's error and the alcohol group's are two ends of one trade, and the six pairs move only with silent odors.

**With any input passed below the knee the gain on the six pairs is gone.** With a tenth of a claw's input passed below the knee, the six pairs' APL effect is below the fit's at every knee ({{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}}, {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee115_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:raw_six_effect ~ +.3f}} at 100, 115 and 130 Hz), and it stays below it with a quarter and with half. The ester group's error is still more than halved with a tenth passed, at losses of {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}} to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee100_g0.1:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, and returns to the fit's as the fraction grows. What comes back with the fraction passed is the fit itself. With half passed below 130 Hz, the setting with the lowest loss, the ester group's error and the weak odors' response fractions are nearly the fit's and the loss is {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:cal_loss ~ .3f}} against the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:cal_loss ~ .3f}}, still above the {{E78/gate.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0.5:loss_limit ~ .3f}} that had been set (second model column). Softening the knee changes little. The five settings nearest the fit were repeated on the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting and on a re-drawn wiring (claw permutation P1), each at its own fit. With the ceiling the six pairs' effect moves by {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:fit1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}; on the re-drawn wiring it moves by {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee100_g0.5:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}} to {{E78/gate.csv:P1_pp_knee115_g0.5_w15:six_raise_vs_start ~ +.3f}}, and the ester group's error is further from zero at each of the five. A knee at half of each odor's largest bouton rate keeps the mean APL effect and has the highest response rate ρ of all the settings, but it leaves the six pairs' effect where the fit has it, doubles the alcohol group's error and raises the pattern part by half (fourth model column). Set higher it cannot hold the response rates: at 0.7 of the largest bouton rate the response rate with APL off stops at {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_rel0.7:ratio ~ .2f}} times that with APL on, outside the band on the ratio, and at 0.85 no somatic threshold gives the fit's responses. No setting did what had been set beforehand, on any of the three fits, so no fit of a knee without a dead zone followed.

**Without the trial noise the six pairs are short by as much.** The table sets a model without noise against recordings that have it. With [the matched trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) put into the fit (the noise matched to the control flies), the distances of both sides can be estimated without their noise from single trials: one minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the cosine between trials of one odor across the same repeats, which assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent. By that estimate the fit has the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_noise_free_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, an APL effect of {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_effect_noise_free ~ +.3f}}, and the flies at {{data:noise_free_six_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:noise_free_six_tnt ~ .3f}}, an effect of {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} (90 % interval {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}). The fit thus has about half the flies' APL effect on these pairs with or without the noise, and the larger shortfall is in their distance with APL on. The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page used until then is not the one to read the model's six pairs by, nor the flies' ([the flies' variability across the three repeats](#repeat-structure)). It assumes that the noise of two odors is independent, and in the recordings and in the model's trial noise alike two odors of one repeat are more alike than across repeats; applied to the fit's trials it puts the six pairs at {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_on ~ .3f}} and {{E81/saved_trials_structure.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;level=match_on;values=graded:six_corrected_off ~ .3f}}, as if they were one odor, which is not what the model does.

**Who is released when APL is removed.** In the fit the {{E78/release.csv:C2_identity:frac_kcs_9+ ~ .0%}} of KCs with nine or more claws take a third of the responses that removing APL adds, and the number of odors per KC is spread more unevenly over the KCs than in the flies ([the input-scaled KC threshold](#input-scaled-threshold)). The hard knees change both. With one, those KCs take a fifth to a quarter of the added responses, and the spread of the number of odors per KC comes down to the flies' or a little under it in both conditions (the two rows above the last of the table). With half of the input passed below the knee both are where the fit has them, and the knee relative to the odor moves the release furthest toward the few-claw KCs while the spread stays the fit's. Selecting responders at the claw thus moves the release off the many-claw KCs, which the input-scaled KC threshold had done at a cost on the main target, but here only with the dead zone that silences the weak odors.

**Realism.** Every setting that held both response rates is inside all four realism bands, and so are both fitted knees, with the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the bands count now, and by the recordings' own criterion, as they did until 2026-11-10. The knee at 0.7 of the odor's largest bouton rate, which did not hold the response rate with APL off, is outside the band on the ratio, and nothing above rests on it. What the hard knees cost lies in what the bands do not hold. ms and B-myr, already under the flies' response fractions in the fit, lose their responses. The largest spike count of a KC to one odor rises from {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off in the fit to {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with the hard knee at 130 Hz at fixed scales: at unchanged response rates, a few KCs driven through a single claw fire much harder. And the parameters are hard to defend. A knee at 100 to 130 Hz lies at {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr100_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:knee_over_top_pn_rate ~ .2f}} to {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr130_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:knee_over_top_pn_rate ~ .2f}} of the model's largest PN rate, so that a claw passing nothing below it is nearly all-or-none, where imaging of single claws shows each claw responding to its own PN input in a graded way and the KC summing several of them (Gruntman and Turner, 2013). The somatic threshold falls from the fit's {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_identity:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} Hz to between {{E78/sweep.csv:C2_pp_knee130_g0:fixed_thr ~ .0f}} and {{E78/partA_scored.csv:thr100_rate0.068_aplboth_k2:fit_fixed_thr ~ .0f}} Hz with a hard knee at 100 Hz or above (last row of the table), and KC–KC inhibition is lowered with it. With half of the input passed below it the knee is mild, with a somatic threshold about half the fit's. No setting is recommended, and the negative result does not depend on the bands, since nothing did what had been set beforehand inside them. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations).

**What follows.** The per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. It had been closed for recruiting the weak odors (the section on the weak-input odors, further up), and a knee near the top of the PN rates does not lower the APL-effect loss in any form: as a hard knee it trades the ester group's error for the alcohol group's and for silent odors, and with input passed below it, or set relative to the odor, it does nothing for the six pairs. Those pairs stay a target of their own, at about half the flies' APL effect and short mostly with APL on. What holds them apart in the flies is then not a transfer of this kind at the claw, nor a fixed change of the input ([above](#input-side)), nor, as far as a static proxy tells, inhibition that follows the calyx space that glomeruli share ([above](#apl-calyx-maps)). What the hard knee did for the release with APL off is kept as a lead: whether responders can be selected at the claw without a dead zone that silences the weak odors is open. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' recording protocol in the model: the best families read as the flies were recorded, and what keeps the response with APL off at the odor's onset {#flies-protocol}

**Read as the flies were recorded, at their 2 s odor pulse and through their response window, the family with the firing ceiling loses its level on the main target at the adaptation it was fitted with: its APL-effect loss on raw spike counts rises by two fifths, most of it in the mean part. It has the level back once the adaptation outlasts the odor. An adaptation that decays over 1 s wears off within a 2 s odor, so that with APL off the KCs that it had held fire again late in the pulse, and those spikes count most in the flies' window. With the adaptation decaying over 3 s, the fit, the literature setting on four wirings and a fit made at the flies' pulse all read what they read at the 0.5 s pulse. Mild depletion at the PN boutons does the same; a slower KC–KC inhibition and a faster or slower APL do not. At the 0.5 s pulse itself the 3 s adaptation leaves the numbers of the family with the ceiling where they were, so that for it the short pulse with that setting stands in for the flies' protocol. The family without a ceiling keeps its match only under the calibrated readout, and a fit at the flies' pulse does not help it on raw counts. The error common to all wirings is made neither by the pulse nor by the window, and the time constant of APL's inhibition does not carry it.** [The flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates) had left the raw-count numbers of the main target tied to the model's 0.5 s pulse, at parameters fitted with that pulse and with every spike counted alike. The flies' responses are neither: a response is the mean of a KC's calcium signal from 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s pulse ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), so that a spike late in the pulse counts for more than one at its onset. The flies' recording protocol in the model read the models that way. Each spike is weighted by the part of an indicator's response to it that falls inside the flies' window, for a response that rises over 0.5 s and decays over 3 s; rises of 0.2 to 1 s and decays of 1 to 5 s were read beside it, the kinetics of the indicator in these recordings not being on hand. The weighted counts are scored raw and through [the calibrated readout](#fn-calibrated-readout), its half-saturation set again on them. Which KCs respond stays the two-spike criterion on the counts, so the response rates and the realism bands do not depend on the reading.

Three things were done. Runs at the 2 s pulse, with both response rates held at each fit's own, were read this way: the breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting on the real wiring (the two fits that the flies' pulse in the model was run on), and each family on four wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle; the ceiling there at its literature setting), scored as the mean over the four. On the two fits, what could keep the response with APL off at the odor's onset was then varied at fixed scales, with both response rates held again: the time constant of the ceiling's adaptation (0.3, 3 and 10 s for its 1 s), depletion of the PN boutons' vesicles at two strengths, a KC–KC inhibition that lasts 0.2 or 1 s for its 0.05 s, and a time constant of APL of 0.01, 0.25 or 1 s for its 0.05 s. What a setting had to do had been set beforehand: bring the fit with the ceiling to a loss of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3:pg_limit ~ .3f}} or less, on spike counts and through the flies' window, inside the realism bands and with spike counts no larger than at the 1 s adaptation. Last, both families were fitted again at the flies' pulse, the one with the ceiling with its adaptation at 3 s.

The breadth-2 APL-effect fit and the same family with the firing ceiling at its stronger setting, on the real wiring: at the model's 0.5 s pulse as fitted, at the flies' 2 s pulse with both response rates held and nothing fitted again, and fitted again at the 2 s pulse. In the first five rows two values are with every spike counted alike / read through the flies' window; in the family with the ceiling the calibrated readout runs to the upper end of its range, where it changes nothing. The eighth row is the model's prediction for the recorded traces: every spike of a responding KC × odor entry is given the indicator's response, the signal is averaged over the responding entries of each condition, and its mean with APL off is divided by its mean with APL on over three parts of the response

**At the adaptation it was fitted with, the ceiling loses its level at the flies' protocol.** At the 0.5 s pulse the fit with the ceiling scores on raw counts below what the breadth-2 fit scores through the calibrated readout, and the flies' window changes next to nothing there, since no spike comes late (fourth model column against the first). At the flies' pulse and through their window its loss is two fifths higher and its mean APL effect a fifth lower, with the pattern part a little higher (fifth model column). That is {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} above the breadth-2 fit's loss through the readout, which hardly moves with the pulse, and still far below that fit's raw counts (second model column). The mean over four wirings at the literature setting rises by as much, more than twice what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}; table below). Late spikes with APL off make this. With APL on nearly every spike of the fit falls in the first half second of the 2 s odor; with APL off a few in a hundred come later (sixth row), from {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_kcs_late ~ .0f}} of the {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_kcs_group ~ .0f}} KCs, and their number grows through the pulse, from {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=bin;key=0.50-0.75:n_spikes ~ .0f}} in the quarter second after 0.5 s to {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=bin;key=1.75-2.00:n_spikes ~ .0f}} in the last quarter second of the odor. The adaptation had been given its time constant of 1 s at a 0.5 s odor, which it outlasted; within a 2 s odor it wears off, and KCs that it had held fire again; with APL on, APL keeps them silent. The flies' window adds to the weight of these spikes because it starts where the pulse ends: the faster the indicator is taken to decay, the higher the loss, from {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r1_d5:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the slowest kinetics read to {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.2_d1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the fastest. With the APL-off spikes later than 0.5 s left out, nothing simulated again, the loss through the flies' window is {{E82/late_leave_out.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;left_out=all:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, the fit's own at the 0.5 s pulse.

Each family as a mean over four wirings (the real one, two claw permutations and one matched shuffle), every wiring with its own fit: the breadth-2 family and the same family with the firing ceiling at its literature setting.
