**An adaptation that outlasts the odor returns the numbers, and so does mild depletion at the boutons.** With the adaptation decaying over 3 s the late spikes with APL off are all but gone, and through the flies' window the fit reads within {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} of what it read at the 0.5 s pulse, with smaller largest spike counts (sixth model column of the first table). At 10 s it reads {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau10:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}, and at 0.3 s, where the adaptation wears off sooner, {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau0.3:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}. The reading no longer depends on the kinetics taken for the indicator ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.2_d1:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the fastest). The literature setting on four wirings, run again with the 3 s adaptation, is back at its loss of the 0.5 s pulse (last column of the second table). The fit made at the flies' pulse with the 3 s adaptation, started from the fit at 0.5 s, ends {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B2_fit0_tau3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .4f}} below the run with held response rates and at the numbers of the 0.5 s pulse in every row, on raw counts and through the readout alike (last column of the first table); having gained less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, it was not repeated on re-drawn wirings. Depletion of the PN boutons' vesicles does at its weaker strength what the longer adaptation does ({{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} through the flies' window, with largest spike counts of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off); at the stronger the loss is {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.03:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}. The other two do not. A KC–KC inhibition that lasts longer removes the late spikes as well, but raises the pattern part, to a loss of {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau0.2:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} at 0.2 s and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} at 1 s. APL's own time constant leaves the spikes with APL off as they are, APL being removed there, and the loss stays between {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.01:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}.

**Without a ceiling only the readout holds.** The breadth-2 family has nothing that bounds the late firing. At the flies' pulse a third of its spikes with APL off come later than 0.5 s and its largest spike counts grow about threefold (sixth and seventh rows of the first table), and through the flies' window its loss on raw counts is two thirds higher than at the 0.5 s pulse on the real wiring and nearly twice as high as a mean over four wirings, with the mean APL effect at less than half. Through the calibrated readout, which takes away most of what the late spikes add to a KC's count, the same runs read within {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:cal_loss ~ .3f}} of the 0.5 s pulse, on the real wiring and as a mean over four wirings. Fitted again at the flies' pulse, the family lowers its loss on raw counts through the flies' window by {{diff:E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss -- E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and leaves the readout's where it was (third model column): its KC–KC inhibition, free in the fit, does not bound the late firing. Of the settings tried on the fit at fixed scales, none brings the loss on raw counts through the flies' window below {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:raw_loss_primary ~ .3f}}, and the two that come nearest, the longest KC–KC inhibition and the stronger depletion, raise the loss through the readout (to {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:cal_loss_primary ~ .3f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_C2_ves0.03:cal_loss_primary ~ .3f}}).

**The common error is made neither by the pulse nor by the window.** In the mean over four wirings of the breadth-2 family the pattern part through the readout is the same at the flies' protocol as at the 0.5 s pulse, and the two groups of the common error keep their signs and sizes: the model's APL effect stays too small among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and too large among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al (last two rows of the second table). On raw counts the pattern part rises with the pulse. Each setting above was also put to the test of [the input side of the error common to all wirings](#input-side), against the same fit's run at the 2 s pulse, and none passes. The largest gain on the pattern part through the readout is {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B3_fit0_ves0.01:pattern_gain ~ .4f}}, from the weaker depletion on the fit with the ceiling, where one draw of the wiring moves the loss by {{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}. The transfer, the share of the common error's squared sum that a setting's change on the real wiring would remove if it were the same on every wiring, is negative at every setting (between {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B5_fit0_taum0.25:transfer_all ~ +.2f}} and {{E82/gate.csv:point_id=B4_fit0_kckctau1:transfer_all ~ +.2f}}): each would add to the common error. The time course of APL's inhibition was the last candidate that the input side had named on the model's side. As a time constant it is closed for this family; an APL that adapts was not run.

**Realism.** With the flies' responses counted in baseline-noise units, as the realism bands count now, every run of this experiment is inside all four bands: the response rates are held, and the number of odors per KC hardly moves with the pulse or the adaptation (lower rows of the first table). Counted by the recordings' own criterion, as until 2026-11-10, the two longer KC–KC inhibitions on the breadth-2 fit leave the band on the number of odors per KC with APL off ({{E82/runs.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau0.2:opk_off_tv_zcrit ~ .3f}} and {{E82/runs.csv:point_id=B4_C2_kckctau1:opk_off_tv_zcrit ~ .3f}} against {{data:tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}); everything else is inside, and nothing above rests on those two. What the result asks to be defended lies outside the bands. It is a KC whose threshold stays raised for 3 s or longer after it has fired: no measurement of a KC's adaptation over seconds is on hand, and the whole-cell recordings from which the ceiling's strength was read used a 0.5 s odor ([footnote](#fn-firing-ceiling)). Without a ceiling the spike counts at the flies' pulse are hard to defend, up to {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=counts:max_count_on ~ .0f}} with APL on and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=rate0.068_aplboth_k2_pulse2_cap3;kernel=counts:max_count_off ~ .0f}} with APL off for one KC and one odor in the fit made at 2 s, where the family with the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation stays at {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=counts:max_count_on ~ .0f}} and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=counts:max_count_off ~ .0f}}. And in every model the response to a 2 s odor is almost all an onset burst: with APL on, {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=on;by=total:share_first_bin ~ .1%}} of the spikes of the fit with the ceiling and {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;condition=on;by=total:share_first_bin ~ .0%}} of the breadth-2 fit's fall in the first quarter second, and whether the flies' KCs fire through a 2 s odor is not in the data on hand. The gain at the flies' protocol thus comes with the adaptation's time constant and costs nothing that the bands hold. As everywhere, the pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations); these three odors have {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=paa:n_late ~ .0f}}, {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=euc:n_late ~ .0f}} and {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=odor;key=-aPine:n_late ~ .0f}} of the {{E82/late_spikes.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse2_held;condition=off;by=total:n_late ~ .0f}} late spikes of the fit with the ceiling.

**What follows.** The raw-count numbers that this page gives for the family with the firing ceiling hold as the flies were recorded on one condition, that the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor. The check that had been left open with the ceiling, whether its effect needs a time constant longer than the odor ([footnote](#fn-firing-ceiling)), is thereby answered: it does. For the family without a ceiling only the calibrated readout holds at either pulse. Two things are then to be decided, and both are choices: whether the firing ceiling, with an adaptation that outlasts the odor, joins the base model, and which reading carries the model's side of the main target, raw counts read as the flies were recorded or the calibrated readout. With the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation the two readings give one number ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} and {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3:cal_loss ~ .3f}} for the fit made at the flies' pulse), so the second choice weighs only if the ceiling stays out. If the ceiling joins with that adaptation, later experiments can stay at the 0.5 s pulse, which takes fewer simulation steps, with each experiment's best fits read once as the flies were recorded. That rests on one more set of runs, the 3 s adaptation at the 0.5 s pulse itself with both response rates held, and they leave the family's numbers in place. On raw counts, every spike counted alike, the fit at the stronger setting reads {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_fit0_tau3;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=fit0_pulse0.5_fixed;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with its 1 s ({{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_fit0_tau10;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} with 10 s); the literature setting as a mean over four wirings reads {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} for {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc;pulse=0.5;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}}, and {{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=2.0;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the flies' pulse with the same adaptation ({{E82/protocol_populations.csv:population=fc_tau3;pulse=2.0;kernel=r0.5_d3:raw_loss ~ .3f}} through the flies' window); and the fit made at the flies' pulse reads {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=B7_D1_held;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at the 0.5 s pulse for {{E82/protocol_readings.csv:point_id=I_B7_D1;kernel=counts:raw_loss ~ .3f}} at its own pulse. Each difference is less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss, the bound set before the runs for the fit and for the four wirings, and all of these runs are inside the realism bands. For this family the 0.5 s pulse with the 3 s adaptation thus stands in for the flies' protocol, and nothing was fitted again. What has to be defended is the adaptation, and how long a KC's threshold stays raised after it has fired is the measurement to ask for; mild depletion at the boutons is the model's other way to the same numbers. The model also gives its side of a question that waits on the recorded traces. With the ceiling and the 3 s adaptation the signal of the responding KCs with APL off is {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=0.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times that with APL on during the pulse and {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=4.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times at the end of the window; without a ceiling the ratio grows from {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=0.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} to {{E82/predicted_ratios.csv:point_id=C2_pulse2_held;kernel=r0.5_d3;signal=resp;t0=4.0:ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} (eighth row of the first table). A ratio that grows after the pulse in the flies would say that their KCs go on firing through an odor when APL output is blocked, which an adaptation of this kind would not allow. What is taken up from here is with the pending work at the end of the page.

### The flies' variability across the three repeats: what the odors of one repeat share, the noise correction it biases, and whether the models read through the trial noise stand {#repeat-structure}

%%% hover
same-repeat gap: The single-trial cosine distance between two different odors presented in different repeats of the panel minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, averaged over odor pairs and recordings. It is positive when the odors of one repeat share part of their trial-to-trial variability.
estimate across repeats: A pair's distance without the trial noise, taken from single trials. One minus the cosine between trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats. It assumes only that the noise of different repeats is independent.
re-specified noise: The model's trial noise set to the flies' two shares. A jitter of each KC's threshold that all odors of a trial share, at the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies', plus a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial that brings the distance between two presentations of one odor to the flies'.
%%%

**In the recordings, two different odors presented in the same repeat of the panel are more alike than the same two odors in different repeats: part of the flies' trial-to-trial variability is shared by the odors of a repeat, and that part is nearly three times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies. About three quarters of it follows the time between the two presentations, mostly a slow drift over the session, and the rest is tied to the repeat itself; neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings follows the order in which the odors were presented. Responses also run down over the session, faster in control flies, so that the ratio of the two response rates rises from the first repeat to the third. The correction for trial-to-trial noise that this page had used takes the noise of two odors to be independent, and it put the distances without noise too low; an estimate that needs only independence between repeats replaces it. The main target, the effect as measured, is not touched: the saved models keep their order against the effect without the noise, and the error common to all wirings is there from the first repeat. The model's trial noise has the wrong make-up, all of it shared between the odors of a trial, but set to the flies' shares it leaves the populations of wirings where they stood, and the firing ceiling's standing with them. What the model does not make is the asymmetry: its odors of one trial are hardly more alike with APL off than with APL on.** Every comparison of a model with the KC data as the data are made passes the model through [trial-to-trial noise](#fn-trial-noise) calibrated on one number, how far apart two presentations of one odor are, and every level quoted without the trial noise came from a correction that takes the noise of different odors to be independent. Each recording holds three repeats of the panel, so both can be checked against the flies. The flies' variability across the three repeats did that from the per-trial responses of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), with 90 % intervals from resampling the recordings. It then scored the saved models against the effect without the noise and read the best families again through a noise with the flies' make-up. No model was fitted.

![Single-trial cosine distances in the recordings' z-scored unit (z in the first panel's title). Left: the mean distance between two presentations of one odor in adjacent repeats and in the first and third repeat, and between two different odors in the same repeat and in different repeats (bars: 90 % intervals over recordings). Middle: the same-repeat gap of each recording, the distance between two odors in different repeats minus that in the same repeat, over all 120 pairs and over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. Right: each pair's distance without the trial noise by the estimate across repeats against the same by the earlier correction (line: equality).](results/E81_repeat_structure/E81_distances_by_kind.png)

**The odors of one repeat share part of their variability, and more of it with APL output blocked.** The same-repeat gap is the distance between two different odors presented in different repeats minus the distance between the same two odors presented in the same repeat, both between single trials. If the variability of two odors' responses were independent it would be zero. It is positive in every recording, {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT) than in control flies (90 % interval {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.lo ~ .1f}} to {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl.hi ~ .1f}}), and largest over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input (table below). The size of the responses does not make it: with every entry reduced to responding or not, the gap is about the same. Of the trial-to-trial variance of a responding KC's response, the part common to that KC's odors within a repeat is {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT3c;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} in control flies and {{E81/variance_parts.csv:units=z;genotype=TNT;level=genotype;cls=responders;statistic=share_shared:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT). The variability also has a slow part: two presentations of one odor are further apart between the first and the third repeat than between adjacent repeats.

**Most of what the odors of a repeat share follows the time between presentations, and the order of the odors does not make the target.** A repeat is one block of the session in which every odor is presented once, so two odors of one repeat are also closer in time than two odors of different repeats, and the order of the presentations tells the two apart: {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT3c;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} of the same-repeat gap in control flies and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=TNT;statistic=separation_share:value ~ .0%}} with APL output blocked (TNT) follows how many presentations apart the two were, and the rest is a step for the same repeat at equal separation (the two rows under the gap in the table above). Most of the first part is a slow drift over the session, two presentations growing less alike with the time between them up to the first repeat against the third (figure below), and both parts are larger with APL output blocked (TNT), by {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=separation_part:value ~ .1f}} and {{E81/order_gap_decomposition.csv:units=z;basis=positions;genotype=ratio;statistic=block_part:value ~ .1f}} times. Across the 120 pairs neither the per-pair APL effect nor the error common to all wirings (under the calibrated readout) follows how far apart the two odors of a pair were presented: their Spearman correlations with the pair's mean separation within a repeat, control flies minus APL output blocked (TNT), are {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:value ~ .2f}}, where 90 % of orders drawn at random with the same reuse of orders give {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_effect_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} and {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal_sep_diff:null_hi ~ .2f}} (the strongest of the twelve such correlations, with the error also on raw counts and the separation also in each genotype alone and in all recordings, is {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:value ~ .2f}}, at p = {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=rho_common_raw_sep_tnt:p_null ~ .2f}}, which the strongest of twelve often reaches by chance). The shift of the per-pair effect that the separations predict has a root mean square of {{E81/order_confound.csv:statistic=confound_rms:value ~ .3f}}, against {{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}} for the floor of the loss. The re-specified noise of the models (below) was matched to the gap as a whole, a jitter per repeat standing in for the drift, so what is concluded below about the models' noise stands.

**Responses run down over the session, and the ratio of the two response rates rises with them.** The response rate of single trials falls from the first repeat to the third in {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT3c;subset=all;level=genotype;statistic=n_recordings_r3_below_r1:value ~ .0f}} of the {{data:n_recordings_ctrl ~ .0f}} control recordings and in {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=all;level=genotype;statistic=n_recordings_r3_below_r1:value ~ .0f}} of the {{data:n_recordings_tnt ~ .0f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), and by more than twice as large a fraction in control flies (last row of the table). The APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio therefore depends on when in the session it is taken: {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1 ~ .2f}} in the first repeat (90 % interval {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r1.hi ~ .2f}}), {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r2 ~ .2f}} in the second and {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3 ~ .2f}} in the third ({{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3.lo ~ .2f}} to {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_r3.hi ~ .2f}}), {{data:repeat_rate_ratio_session ~ .2f}} over all single trials. The two recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) whose distances stand apart from the other six ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)) are the two that do not run down: from the first repeat to the third their response rate changes by {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=strong2;level=genotype;statistic=rate_change_r3_vs_r1:value ~ +.2f}} of its value in the first repeat, against {{E81/rundown.csv:units=noise;criterion=bands;genotype=TNT;subset=typical6;level=genotype;statistic=rate_change_r3_vs_r1:value ~ +.2f}} for the six.

![The run-down over the three repeats, with single trials counted above the realism bands' threshold in baseline-noise units (90 % intervals over recordings; thin lines: single recordings). Left: the response rate by repeat. Middle: the mean amplitude of the responding entries. Right: the APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio by repeat, over all recordings and with only the six recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) that are alike, against the realism band on the ratio (grey).](results/E81_repeat_structure/E81_rundown.png)

**The earlier noise correction is biased, and the target is not.** The correction divided each pair's cosine by the two odors' signal norms, on the assumption that the noise adds nothing to the product of two different odors' responses. What the odors of a repeat share does add to that product, and the correction counted it as similarity between the odors. It therefore put the distances too low, most with APL output blocked (TNT), where the shared part is larger, and so the mean APL effect too high. The estimate across repeats uses only products of trials from different repeats, which that shared part does not enter: one minus the cosine between single trials of the two odors from different repeats, divided by the geometric mean of the two odors' cosines between their own trials across the same repeats.

The KC data as measured, by the earlier noise correction and without the trial noise by the estimate across repeats (the recordings' z-scored unit; 90 % intervals over recordings in parentheses)

Without the trial noise the per-pair APL effect is close to the effect as measured: across the 120 pairs the two have a Spearman correlation of {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_rho_measured ~ .2f}} and a root mean squared difference of {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=effect;estimator=noise_free;statistic=rms_diff_from_measured:value ~ .3f}}, well under the floor of the loss; its own floor is a little higher and its ceiling the same (last two rows of the table). The main target therefore stands as it is defined, on the three-trial means. What changes is the level quoted for a model without noise. The mean distances are higher than the earlier correction gave, the mean effect is hardly above the measured one, and over the six pairs with near-identical ORN input the effect without the noise is smaller than as measured, not larger. The estimate has a limit of its own. With APL output blocked (TNT) the mean distance estimated from adjacent repeats is {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:value ~ .3f}} above the one estimated from the first against the third repeat ({{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:lo ~ .3f}} to {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=tnt;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:hi ~ .3f}}; in control flies the two agree, {{E81/noise_free_summary.csv:units=z;values=graded;side=ctrl;estimator=adjacent_minus_first_third;statistic=mean:value ~ +.3f}}), so there the slow drift does not cancel completely.

**The saved models keep their order, and the error common to all wirings is there from the first repeat.** Scored against the effect without the noise, nearly every saved model's loss is a little higher and the order is the same: over the {{lit:1058 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (the number of variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv with both losses on raw counts)}} saved models the losses against the two effects have a Spearman correlation of {{lit:0.999 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (Spearman correlation of raw_measured_loss with raw_noise_free_loss over the variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv)}} on raw spike counts and {{lit:0.991 # results/E81_repeat_structure/comparison_table.md, section B1 (Spearman correlation of cal_measured_loss with cal_noise_free_loss over the variant rows of by_variant_noise_free.csv)}} under the calibrated readout, and the ten lowest are the same ten. Nor does the session's history make the error common to all wirings. The per-pair APL effect taken within one repeat, from single trials of both genotypes, has the same mean in each repeat ({{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r1 ~ +.3f}}, {{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r2 ~ +.3f}} and {{data:repeat_apl_effect_mean_r3 ~ +.3f}}), and its Spearman correlation with the common error across the 120 pairs is as strong in the first repeat as in the third ({{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=1:value ~ .2f}}, {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=2:value ~ .2f}} and {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=3:value ~ .2f}}; {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=rho_common_cal;repeat=session:value ~ .2f}} for the three-trial means; negative because the error is the model's effect minus the flies'). An error built up by the run-down would be weaker in the first repeat. The size of the effect's part along the error is {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:value ~ .2f}} times larger in the third repeat than in the first, with an interval that includes no change ({{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:lo ~ .2f}} to {{E81/effect_by_repeat.csv:statistic=proj_common_cal_ratio_3_over_1;repeat=all:hi ~ .2f}}).

**With the flies' shares in the model's noise, the populations of wirings stay where they stood.** The trial noise put into the models is one draw per KC and trial, applied to the KC's threshold for all odors of the trial, so all of it is of the shared kind. At the level that matches the flies' distance between two presentations of one odor, the breadth-2 APL-effect fit has a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_on ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_off ~ .3f}} with APL off, where the flies have {{data:repeat_gap_ctrl ~ .3f}} and {{data:repeat_gap_tnt ~ .3f}}. The noise was therefore re-specified with the flies' two shares. The shared jitter was lowered to the level at which the model's same-repeat gap is the flies' (for that fit a standard deviation of {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:sigma ~ .3f}} of the threshold with APL on and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:sigma ~ .3f}} with APL off, against {{E81/jitter_at_flies_gap.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:sigma_matched_on ~ .3f}} in the pipeline), by interpolation between saved runs of the pipeline without noise, at half its matched jitter and at the matched level, and a factor drawn independently for every KC, odor and trial was added until the distance between two presentations of one odor was the flies' as well. The two populations of four wirings that had been read through the pipeline, the breadth-2 family without and with the firing ceiling at its literature setting ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), were scored again through this noise.

Through the re-specified noise the loss of the population without the ceiling moves by {{diff:E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss -- E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ +.3f}} and that of the population with it by {{diff:E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss -- E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ +.3f}}, both under half of what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}), and the ceiling's lead over the family without it stays inside that as well. Under the calibrated readout the two populations read {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}}, where through the pipeline they read {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=cal;unit=z;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}}: the two swap places, by less than one draw of the wiring moves the loss there ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=cal:sd_single ~ .3f}}). Against the flies' effect in baseline-noise units, where every model is short on the mean, the losses on raw counts are higher under either noise and in the same order ({{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} through the re-specified noise, {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=noise;kind=present_match_on:loss ~ .3f}} through the pipeline). The numbers read through the pipeline therefore stand, and with them the reading that the firing ceiling gives no clear gain on raw counts once flies and trials are both in the model. A second form of the independent part, a jitter of the threshold drawn anew for every presentation and run as simulations for the two fits on the real wiring, gives the same reading: {{E81/per_presentation.csv:group=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=presentation:loss ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit, where the factor gives {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}}, and {{E81/per_presentation.csv:group=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=presentation:loss ~ .3f}} and {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E69-rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:loss ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling.

**Two statistics depend on the make-up of the noise more than the loss does.** One is the effect on the six pairs with near-identical ORN input. With the noise removed from both sides by the estimate across repeats, the population without the ceiling has an APL effect of {{E81/populations.csv:group=breadth-2 four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix_noise_free:six_effect ~ +.3f}} on them and the population with it {{E81/populations.csv:group=firing-ceiling four;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix_noise_free:six_effect ~ +.3f}}, against the flies' {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six ~ +.3f}} ({{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.lo ~ +.3f}} to {{data:noise_free_apl_effect_six.hi ~ +.3f}}): a little under two thirds of the flies' effect, where the single fit has about half ([the high per-claw knee without a dead zone](#claw-knee)), so these pairs stay a target of their own. The other is the block. The pipeline's jitter had cut the block of the reference family's fits by more than half ([above](#other-targets)). Read again through the re-specified noise, the same fits keep most of their block, and the fit that lost most through the pipeline keeps most (table below). For these three fits the shared jitter with APL on lies below the lowest saved level and is interpolated from the run without noise; their re-fits to a larger block, whose levels lie between saved runs, read {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E48-thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_block0.072_k2_cap3_exact;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:block ~ +.3f}} to {{E81/mix_scores.csv:name=E48-thr70_gain1.5_rate0.068_block0.072_k2_cap3_exact;readout=raw;unit=z;kind=mix:block ~ +.3f}}. The two populations, whose block is smaller to begin with, keep it through the shared jitter alone and lose part of it to the independent noise. In every row of the table the model's block stays below the flies'.

**What the model does not make.** Two features of the flies' variability are in the model under no noise that was tried. The first is the asymmetry between the conditions. In the flies the same-repeat gap is {{data:repeat_gap_ratio_tnt_ctrl ~ .1f}} times larger with APL output blocked (TNT). In the model, a jitter per KC gives a gap with APL off that is {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times the gap with APL on for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=F1;condition=both:gap_ratio_off_on ~ .2f}} times for the fit with the ceiling, and the re-specified noise reaches the flies' two gaps only by taking a larger jitter with APL off than with APL on. A slow change of the whole population does not make the asymmetry either. A factor on every KC's threshold of 0.8, 1 and 1.2 in three successive trials, a wider swing than the flies' run-down amounts to (for the fit with the ceiling the control flies' run-down corresponds to a threshold that rises by a factor of {{E81/rundown_axes.csv:unit=z;experiment=E69_kc_firing_ceiling;tag=rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2;repeat=0:thr_change_first_to_last ~ .2f}} from the first repeat to the third), leaves a same-repeat gap of {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=on:gap ~ .3f}} with APL on and {{E81/shared_state.csv:model=C2;triplet=0.8/1/1.2;readout=raw;condition=acute_off:gap ~ .3f}} with APL off in the breadth-2 fit. The second is how alike the responders of one repeat are with APL off. With every entry reduced to responding or not, the same-repeat gap with APL off is {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the breadth-2 fit and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} for the fit with the ceiling through the re-specified noise, against the flies' {{data:repeat_gap_binary_tnt ~ .3f}}, and the same with the jitter per presentation ({{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}} and {{E81/per_presentation_checks.csv:model=F1;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:bin_gap ~ .3f}}); with APL on it is close to the flies' ({{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:bin_gap ~ .3f}} against {{data:repeat_gap_binary_ctrl ~ .3f}}). The shortfall is thus a property of which KCs the model has responding with APL off and not of how the noise is drawn: the flies' larger shared variability with APL output blocked (TNT) has no counterpart in the model.

**Realism.** No model is changed or fitted here, so every model stands in the realism bands where it stood; the re-specified noise asks less of a KC than the pipeline does (a threshold that differs between repeats with a standard deviation of {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=on:sigma ~ .0%}} of its value with APL on and {{E81/mix_checks.csv:model=C2;readout=raw;unit=z;condition=acute_off:sigma ~ .0%}} with APL off for the breadth-2 fit, against {{E81/jitter_at_flies_gap.csv:folder=E72_wiring_population;model=E67-rate0.068_aplboth_k2_cap3:sigma_matched_on ~ .0%}} in the pipeline), and the flies' APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio is inside its band in each of the three repeats, the band's reference value being a mean over a session that the model does not have. All model numbers here are of the model's 0.5 s odor pulse ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)), and the model's pairs with paa, euc and -aPine rest on [ORN input at another concentration](#fn-concentrations), as everywhere; the six pairs with near-identical ORN input include none of those odors, and the flies' side of this subsection uses no ORN input.

**What follows.** Where this page gives a level of the KC data without the trial noise, it is now the estimate across repeats, and the earlier correction is named where a result was made with it (the re-fits to the corrected block and one reading of the table of readings). The main target stays the effect as measured, with its floor and its ceiling. The pipeline stays the way a model is read as the data are made: its noise is all shared between the odors of a trial where only part of the flies' is, but with the flies' shares no population of wirings moved by as much as one draw of the wiring moves the loss, so the numbers read through it stand. The block is the statistic for which the make-up of the noise matters, and a block read through the pipeline is a block under more shared jitter than the flies' repeats support. The six pairs with near-identical ORN input stay a target of their own, at a little under two thirds of the flies' effect once the noise is removed from both sides. The order in which the odors were presented changes none of this: it does not make the target, and it shows most of what the odors of a repeat share to be a slow drift over the session. One thing is open. A trial noise for the model that is right where the present one is not needs a source of shared variability that is larger without APL, most of it such a drift, so a slow change in a subset of the KCs or in the input; the same-repeat gap of the responders with APL off is the statistic to hold it to. It is with the pending work at the end of the page.

## How close the best models have come to the KC data, over the run

The plot below tracks, for nine of the statistics used throughout this page, how far the best model found so far had closed the gap between the first measured model and the KC data, against the time each experiment finished. Two of the lines are the main target: the APL-effect loss, for which lower is better and 100 % is the data's floor ({{data:apl_effect_rmse_floor ~ .3f}}, the loss a model with the flies' true effect would still show, not zero), and ρ on the per-pair APL effect (ceiling {{data:apl_effect_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}}). These two lines count only variants inside the realism bands (a response rate with APL on of 0.045 to 0.085, an APL-off / APL-on response rate ratio of 1.6 to 2.9, a response rate ρ with APL on of at least 0.37, and a distribution of the number of odors each KC responds to within {{data:noise_ctrl_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}} of the control flies' with APL on and within {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .2f}} of that of the flies with APL output blocked (TNT) with APL off, the flies' responses counted in [baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units); a variant whose responses were not saved is held to the first two), so that a loss lowered through the response rates, or by gathering the responses in few KCs, does not show as progress. The fourth band decides one step of the loss line. Before the APL-effect fits the line stood at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the joint fit to both matrices run at breadth exponent 3, which is at the limit of that band with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E10_joint_fit;tag=k3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, the band's own value to three decimals); the one variant on the plot's terms with a lower loss, breadth-weighted APL alone on the bouton baseline ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E12_breadth_apl;tag=spikes_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), is outside that band with APL off. The APL-effect fits took the line to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the lowest loss on raw counts among [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) without a glomerulus gain: the first joint fit's family at breadth exponent 3, fitted on raw counts at the flies' response rate and scored on all four bands and inside the one on odors per KC with APL off ({{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:opk_off_tv ~ .3f}} from the flies' distribution, against a band of {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_tv_max ~ .3f}}). It is one of the fits that give up KC–KC inhibition and the block for a larger mean effect, with APL→bouton at {{E67/comparison.csv:kind=fit;tag=rate0.068_aplraw_k3_cap3:aplpn_factor_vs_e3 ~ .2f}} times the baseline's against a bound of three. The line is on deterministic runs: there the breadth-2 fit of the best-models table, which keeps both, stands at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E67_apl_effect_fits;tag=rate0.068_aplcal_k2_cap3:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, and through the matched trial noise the breadth-3 fit holds its loss while the breadth-2 fit falls narrowly below it ([the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)). The firing ceiling then took the line to {{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the breadth-2 fit made again with a firing ceiling at its stronger setting, inside all four bands ([the firing ceiling for the KCs](#firing-ceiling)). The line now ends at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, the same fit made once more with the response-rate terms of its loss against the flies' response rates counted in baseline-noise units, inside all four bands as well ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)); that last step, of {{diff:E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse -- apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, is smaller than what one draw of the wiring moves the loss on raw counts ({{E72/spread.csv:readout=raw:sd_single ~ .3f}}). The best-models table carries the fit at the literature setting ({{E69/stats_variants.csv:rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.04142t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}), the one whose spike counts agree with whole-cell recordings of KCs; through the matched trial noise the two settings score alike, both below every fit without a ceiling. The line of ρ on the per-pair APL effect ends with a small step, from {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E76_data_side_target;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .3f}} to {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E82_flies_protocol;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_spearman ~ .3f}}, taken by a fit of the same family made at the flies' 2 s odor pulse with the ceiling's adaptation at 3 s, inside all four bands ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)); on the loss line that fit stands at {{apl_effect/by_variant.csv:folder=E82_flies_protocol;tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t3000_k2_pulse2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_rmse ~ .3f}}, level with the line's end. That experiment's points are of fits made at the flies' pulse; every point before them is of the model's 0.5 s pulse. For the other seven, 100 % is the data's value, or its measurement ceiling where the data set one (the agreement between two halves of the recordings): ρ on odor-odor distances between the model and the KC data with APL on (the control matrix, ceiling {{data:ctrl_ceiling ~ .2f}}) and with APL off (the APL output blocked (TNT) matrix, ceiling {{data:tnt_ceiling ~ .2f}}), the fruity × small-ester block ({{data:block ~ +.3f}}), the per-odor response rate ρ with the control flies (ceiling {{data:ctrl_rate_rho_ceiling ~ .2f}}), the structure vs wild-type somata ({{data:ctrl_struct_wt ~ .2f}}), and the natural-source alignment of the APL-on residual ({{data:ctrl_vcf ~ .2f}}) and of the APL-off residual ({{data:tnt_vcf ~ .2f}}); the APL-off / APL-on response-rate ratio is left out because the first measured model already sat at the data's {{data:rate_ratio_fraction ~ .1f}}, as most tuned acute-knockout models do. Each experiment contributes its best variant on each statistic separately (so the points on different lines are usually different models), among variants tuned near the 5 % operating point and excluding the oracle constructions, the random or shuffled wirings, the level-matched input controls and the control of the sign of the input-scaled KC threshold (a power of −0.5); the last column of the best-models table carries the oracle gain, so it is not on the plot. The staircase is the best so far; hover a point for the experiment and the model behind it, click a legend entry to hide a line.

Two things the lines say that the sections above say in words: the block and the two structure statistics were closed early and by different models (the block by breadth-weighted APL with KC–KC inhibition, the structure by the coincidence rule and the per-claw threshold), while ρ on odor-odor distances with the two matrices and response rate ρ have moved by a fifth of their gap at most, and since the joint fits the lines have hardly moved, because the models that close one gap reopen another, until the APL-effect fits put the APL-effect loss first in the loss and lowered it, and the firing ceiling for the KCs lowered it again; the best single model on all statistics at once is in the table of the section before.

## Experiments running or not yet run, and what each would tell us

Pending work is judged first on the main target: what an experiment is expected to do to [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect), to its mean part and to its pattern part, inside the realism bands, comes before its bearing on any other statistic. The band on the number of odors each KC responds to is the one a model's operating point bears on: a model tuned to 5 % starts at a disadvantage on it. [The APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits) are inside all four bands at the flies' response rate, so a new mechanism is compared with them, at that response rate and under both definitions of the model's side, with the per-KC reading beside them.

- **The firing ceiling's adaptation, the reading of the model's side, and the recordings behind the target.** Read as the flies were recorded, at their 2 s pulse and through their response window, the family with the firing ceiling keeps its raw-count match to the main target only if the ceiling's adaptation outlasts the odor, and the family without a ceiling keeps its match only under the calibrated readout ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). Two choices follow and are still to be made: whether the ceiling, with such an adaptation, joins the base model, and which reading carries the model's side of the main target. If the ceiling joins, raw counts read as the flies were recorded and the calibrated readout give nearly the same numbers, and later experiments can stay at the 0.5 s pulse with their best fits read once as the flies were recorded; if it stays out, the calibrated readout carries the comparison with the flies, and every raw-count number is reported as one of the 0.5 s pulse. The first case rested on one more set of runs, the 3 s adaptation at the 0.5 s pulse itself, and they leave the numbers of that pulse where they are: the short pulse with that setting stands in for the flies' protocol, and neither a new fit of the family nor the flies' pulse in the base is needed. What would settle the first choice is a measurement, how long a KC's threshold stays raised after it has fired: an adaptation that lasts seconds supports the ceiling as it now has to be set, and one that is over within the odor leaves the bound on the late firing to be found elsewhere, with depletion at the PN boutons as the candidate that the model has. If the reading moves to the flies' protocol, the trial noise and the per-KC reading have to be made for fits at the 2 s pulse, which they do not take yet. On the data's side one question waits on the experimenter: which recordings make the target. Recordings of the panel that the target does not use exist, and whether they can serve as a test is with the experimenter, who is checking their quality. If they give the same effect, the target is replicated and the common error is not an accident of the recordings used; if the target moves by more than its floor, every model is scored again. When in the response the flies' APL effect is made is the next item.
- **The time course of the APL effect in the flies' traces.** Every value of the KC data on this page is a mean over one window of each response, 2 to 8 s after the onset of a 2 s odor pulse, and [the reading of the models as the flies were recorded](#flies-protocol) had to assume how fast the indicator rises and decays. The frame-by-frame traces of the 19 recordings are now being read, for four questions. The first is when in the response the per-pair APL effect and the two groups' parts of the error common to all wirings are made. If they are the same from the first second of the odor to the end of the window, with the trial-to-trial noise removed window by window, the time within a response is closed as a source of the common error on the data's side, as it is on the model's side; if a window lowers the error or the two groups part ways, the window becomes a stated choice of the target, and the error is read against the model's own windows. The second is the indicator's kinetics in these recordings. If the signal decays over many seconds, the flies' window weighs all spikes of the pulse about equally, the reading through an assumed fast indicator overstates what late firing costs, and the models' numbers at the flies' protocol are restated with the measured kinetics; if it decays within the window, the assumed reading stands. The third is the model's prediction for the traces: the signal with APL output blocked (TNT), relative to the control flies', stays level through the response where something holds the firing to the odor's onset, and grows after the pulse where nothing does (the first table of [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). A ratio that grows in the flies as in the family without such a bound would say that their KCs go on firing through the odor; a level ratio excludes that family's late firing on the traces alone, whatever its loss, and says how long an adaptation the flies' own responses ask for. The fourth is whether the recordings behind the target were all measured alike. If the rise and decay of the responses are the same in every recording, the recordings with the largest APL effect differ from the others only in strength; if theirs differ, which recordings make the target becomes a question for the experimenter, with that evidence beside [the recordings one by one](#data-side).
- **The input and APL's glomerulus profile fitted on several wirings at once.** Two earlier experiments each found, on the hemibrain wiring alone, a change that lowers the error common to all wirings there: a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli of a KC's claws ([above](#glomerulus-profile)) and an input searched glomerulus by glomerulus for each odor ([above](#input-side)). Neither was shown to hold beyond that wiring. The profile was never run on a re-drawn wiring, and the searched input, at the size the search gave it, did not lower the error of the mean over wirings on recordings it had not seen. The saved runs add that such an input changes the distances of every wiring alike, and that its change of the APL effect points partly the way the unseen recordings ask but is too large. The experiment therefore fits both kinds of change to the mean over four wirings and one half of the recordings, and tests them on four other wirings and on the other half, at a size reduced by the share of one half's pattern that the other half reproduces. If the profile passes, where APL acts, by the glomeruli of a KC's claws, becomes the next mechanism, and it is set against the connectomes' APL synapses. If the input passes, the common error can be reached through what reaches the KCs, and the next step is a measurement of the ORN or PN responses that the search changes most, not a mechanism. If neither passes, the test says why. A change that carries to other wirings on the recordings it was fitted to, but not to the other recordings, has fitted the recordings' noise, and the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) are then what limits the pattern. A change that does not carry to other wirings has fitted the wirings' draws. In both cases static changes at the level of the glomeruli are closed in their fitted form. A change that passes is then read at the flies' pulse and through the trial noise.
- **The open measurement question** is the ORN responses of the oracle glomeruli to ms, paa, B-myr, euc and 1-8ol at Yang's concentrations; after the Hallem-input test it is two glomeruli first, DL1's response to ms and DM6's to paa at 10^-3, which would decide whether those two odors' deficit is in the input, while B-myr's and euc's stay open. The decomposition of the gain adds that its structural part needs a measurement of a different kind: DC2's drive onto the KCs relative to its ORN response ([above](#gain-decomposition)). The bounded-input oracle adds, for paa at 10^-3, VL2a (searched up), DP1m and DM4 (searched down) and DM6, which the search lowers where Hallem's data raise it, so that one glomerulus tests the two against each other; for B-myr, whose recording is already at Yang's concentration, the question is whether DM1 at half and DC1 and D at twice the recorded response are within the spread of the ORN recordings ([above](#gap-pairs)).
- **Model and readout changes still worth making:** a saturating APL unit nonlinearity, a calcium readout with the indicator's kinetics (the static saturating readout is done, [above](#readout), so is the recordings' per-KC normalization without the kinetics, [above](#per-kc-normalization), and so is a reading over the flies' response window with kinetics that were assumed, [above](#flies-protocol); the kinetics of the indicator in these recordings are what is missing), measured ORN time courses, real weights for the KCs of unknown type, and, from the weak-odor analyses, better-constrained ORN input for ms, B-myr, euc, paa and 1-8ol (concentrations and glomerular profiles; Hallem's receptor data, [tried above](#hallem-input), cover ms and paa but not B-myr or euc, and at ten times Yang's concentration). From the compressive readout: a mechanism that makes the block through which KCs respond, joined to the best models' mean effect and scored under the compressive and the binarized readout; and, as a constraint that no readout touches and that is now one of [the realism bands](#apl-effect), the number of odors each KC responds to with APL off (the reference model leaves {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:odors_0_off ~ .0%}} of its KCs silent and has {{E65/model_amplitude.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:odors_8plus_off ~ .0%}} responding to eight or more of the 16 odors, against {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_0 ~ .0%}} and {{data:noise_tnt_odors_per_kc_8plus ~ .0%}} in the flies with APL output blocked (TNT), at nearly the same overall response rate). From the per-odor profile of the APL effect ([above](#apl-effect-parts)): the number-of-odors breadth in a fit of the main target (the exponent of the spike-total breadth has been fitted in the first joint fit's family, where the loss is lowest near 2, [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits)); for the pair-specific part, gain sets without DM5 fitted and scored on it, and a form of the breadth weighting that keeps APL off the high-firing KCs without leaving the distance between two odors to the few KCs they share through one glomerulus; and no per-odor APL rule fitted to the response rates, which the per-odor APL oracle shows would not move the main target. From the low end of the readout ([above](#readout)): the amplitudes of the responses with APL off as a second constraint for later fits of the main target, beside the number of odors per KC and like it independent of how the target is defined (with APL output blocked (TNT) {{data:tnt_share_z_above_4 ~ .1%}} of the flies' KC × odor entries are above 4 z and their responders' mean amplitude is {{data:tnt_resp_amp_mean_z ~ .2f}} z, about as in the control flies; the reference model with APL off, read as in the table of amplitudes there, has {{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:share_above_4_off ~ .1%}} and {{E68/partB_amplitude.csv:model=ref40;config=floor_noise:resp_amp_mean_off ~ .2f}} z); and, for the recordings, what makes the negative values, now that how the trial means are made is known (each KC's trace z-scored over the whole recording, the 5 s before the odor as the baseline, 0.7 of the neuropil subtracted; [the footnote on baseline-noise units](#fn-baseline-noise-units)), which leaves the order of the odors within a repeat to look at (the order is on hand now and has not been read for them; what it and the repeats show of the flies' variability is [above](#repeat-structure)), since the negative values, which repeat across trials, make up a fifth of the control flies' entries ({{data:ctrl_share_z_below_m025 ~ .0%}} below −0.25 z). From [the APL-effect fits](#apl-effect-fits): the three fits that went through the trial noise run again on further seeds of the noise, since on raw counts the breadth-2 fit's margin over the breadth-3 fit is about the difference between the two noise levels (if the margin holds over seeds, the breadth-2 family is the lowest under both definitions; if it does not, raw counts do not separate a model that has the block from one that gave it up, and the block has to be held as a target of its own); the breadth-2 fit repeated on shuffled draws of the wiring, the replication the earlier joint fits were given, has been run as the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings ([above](#wiring-population)): its loss returns on the draws, so the family is the model to build on (what follows from it is listed further down); a mechanism that spreads the recruitment with APL off over more KCs, which neither a term on odors per KC in the loss nor the fitted parameters do, was the next step and has been run as the input-scaled KC threshold ([above](#input-scaled-threshold); what follows from it is listed further down); and, for the block under the readout, the mechanism acting on which KCs respond that is listed above, now with the breadth-2 fit as its base, since a block term in the loss does not raise that fit's block under the readout. From the high-firing KCs that survive APL ([above](#high-firing-kcs)): a carrier of the block that is not a few over-driven KCs, which the mechanisms acting on the set of responding KCs are, joined to a model without such cells; the single pseudo-recordings of a model through the matched trial noise, scored as single pairs of recordings were, have been run since, and the breadth-2 fit is already as close to the data's mean as a single pair of recordings is ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)). The route through the weak-input odors' input is not taken up, because the archived models that already take it change the survivors and the mean effect little: in the reference model as fitted at 5 %, leaving DP1m's gain out leaves {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DP1m:n_survivors ~ .0f}} survivors against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full:n_survivors ~ .0f}} with all eight glomeruli gained and a mean APL effect on raw counts of {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__loo_DP1m:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E39_gain_decomposition;tag=thr40__full:raw__mean ~ +.3f}}; with every odor's input scaled until its response rate with APL on is the flies', the reference model has {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E62_rate_oracle;tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:n_survivors ~ .0f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:n_survivors ~ .0f}} and {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E62_rate_oracle;tag=R_thr40_gain1.5_on:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} against {{E70/per_variant.csv:folder=E44_operating_point;tag=thr40_gain1.5_rate0.068_k2_cap3:raw__mean ~ +.3f}} (the flies' {{data:apl_effect_mean ~ +.3f}}). No further re-draws of single cells' claws are planned. From the firing ceiling for the KCs ([above](#firing-ceiling)): whether the ceiling joins the base model, and at which strength, which needs one number, the largest spike count of a fly KC to a 0.5 s odor (the bound used is a reading of the recordings' means and standard deviations; through the trial noise the literature setting is as good as the stronger one, so it is the setting to adopt if the ceiling joins); the literature setting fitted on re-drawn wirings has been run ([above](#wiring-population)): the gain on raw counts returns on each of the three wirings tried, and the mean over wirings with the ceiling scores on raw counts what it scores under the readout; the same mean has since been read through the trial noise ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), where it is level with the mean of the family without a ceiling, so that the gain on raw counts belongs to the model without noise and to single wirings; the block and the natural-source alignment on a base with the ceiling, which takes them away with the strong responders as the readout does, so that the carrier of the block listed above has to work on that base; the recruitment with APL off, which the ceiling leaves as it was and the input-scaled KC threshold moves off the many-claw KCs at a cost on the main target ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)); and, if the ceiling is adopted, a less schematic adaptation (two time constants, or synaptic depression at the claws); the check that its effect does not need a time constant longer than the odor has been made, and at the flies' 2 s pulse it does need one ([the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)). From the input-scaled KC threshold ([above](#input-scaled-threshold)): which KCs carry the APL effect, which has been run as the APL effect split by odors per KC ([above](#apl-effect-by-class); what follows from it is listed further down); the family with the firing ceiling and the scaling at a small power under the reading of the per-KC normalization of the recordings, which the same experiment fitted and where the scaling cost nothing only because the fit left the two-spike operating point, so that the fit is to be made again with its response-rate terms on the two-spike criterion, as fits now are, if that reading is taken up for fits (if the scaling then costs less than a draw of the wiring moves the loss, the ceiling with the scaling is the candidate base and is compared on re-drawn wirings, where it has not been run; if it costs more, it stays out under every reading); a fit with the scaling and a term on the number of odors per KC in the loss, to see what the main target costs when the broad responders are held at the flies' share; other forms of the scaling (a threshold set from each KC's drive over a reference set of odors, a normalization of the drive per glomerulus), which were not tried and matter only if a fit with the scaling is taken up; and, for the realism bands, whether the band on the number of odors per KC should also hold the spread of that number, which in the breadth-2 family is above every recording's on all eight wirings it has been fitted on and which the band as defined does not see. From the APL-effect fit on re-drawn wirings ([above](#wiring-population)): whether the main target is defined on a mean over wirings read through the trial noise, as the data's mean is one over flies and trials, which is a choice about the target like the readout (until it is made, that mean is given beside the single-wiring number, and two fits closer than about the draw term are compared on the real wiring and at least two re-drawn ones); the error common to all wirings as the target of the next mechanisms, the too-small APL effect among the esters and on the pairs of eb, 1-8ol, IaA and ep above all, read beside the APL effect split by odors per KC, which is reported for each fit and not fitted ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)) (a mechanism that lowers that error on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones moves the family toward the floor, while one that lowers the loss on the real wiring alone has fitted that wiring's own remainder); the first such mechanism, a profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli, has been run and does not carry that error ([above](#glomerulus-profile); what follows from it is listed further down); recruitment at the weakest input in the family without a per-claw threshold, ma at 10^-7 first, through a per-claw transfer that adds drive at low input in place of a softened threshold (if it brings ma to the flies' fraction at no cost on the 16-odor panel, the low-concentration recordings become constraints the family meets; if it costs there, they stay a regime of their own); and, of the two checks on wirings that were left, the mean over wirings with the firing ceiling read through the trial noise has been run ([above](#glomerulus-profile)), and the input-scaled KC threshold on re-drawn wirings beside the ceiling fits made there has not. From the per-KC normalization of the recordings ([above](#per-kc-normalization)): which definition the model's side of the main target is held to, raw counts, the calibrated readout or the per-KC reading, the one of the three that is taken from how the recordings were made (the reading and the readout order the models alike, so the choice moves the numbers more than the ranking; until it is made every fit is reported under all three, with its response-rate terms on the two-spike count); a mechanism, or a term of the readout, by which a KC that responds to many odors responds more strongly to each of them, as the flies' KCs do and the models' do not (if a model gets that growth inside the realism bands, its amplitudes with APL off, listed above as a second constraint, and its units under the reading come nearer the flies' together; if the growth can only be had with the strong firing that the firing ceiling removes, it belongs to what the calcium signal adds to the spike count, and the readout is the place for it); the reading with the indicator's kinetics, since a response in the recordings outlasts its window and the loss of the family without the ceiling moves with that share while the family with the ceiling does not; the data side of the main target, which is still computed from the z-scored values, has been measured ([above](#data-side)): the flies' per-pair APL effect, its floor and its split by odors per KC were computed with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units, beside the effect as measured, and only the mean effect depends on the unit, so the pattern part and the order of the models stand and the unit is a choice about the mean, like the readout (what follows from it is listed further down); and, before the amplitudes, response rates or numbers of odors per KC of Remy's wild-type megamat KC recordings are compared with these, a check of how those recordings were normalized. From the APL effect split by odors per KC ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)): the split of the APL effect over the classes of KCs is reported for every later fit beside the realism bands, as a statistic of its own and not as a term of a loss, since the family that is asked for it pays on the total and its pattern part does not move; the pattern part is looked for in the per-pair errors that remain whatever the classes do, which the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition took up ([above](#glomerulus-profile); what follows from it is listed further down); and, if the main target stays in the recordings' z-scored units, what would bring the class at four to seven odors to the flies' is a mechanism that makes the KCs of that class carry less of the overlap between odors with APL on, which is where the models differ from the flies in it (in the archive a per-claw threshold and the input-scaled threshold do that, each with a higher pattern part; if a mechanism does it on re-drawn wirings without that cost, the model comes nearer the flies in which KCs carry the effect at no price on the target, and if none does, the class stays a known difference that the total does not need); with each KC's responses in baseline-noise units the flies' class at four to seven carries none of the effect, and there is nothing to bring the models' class to ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). From the glomerulus profile of APL inhibition ([above](#glomerulus-profile)): the common error, a too-small APL effect among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms and a too-large one among 1-8ol, 1-5ol, 1-6ol and 6al on every wiring, stays the target of the next mechanisms. They were looked for first in what reaches the KCs, which has been run as the input side of the error common to all wirings ([above](#input-side); what follows from it is listed further down). A fixed profile of APL's weight over the glomeruli did not carry it, and the few saved models with less than half of it, the oracle co-responder suppression apart, change the input and not APL: a weaker antennal-lobe normalization and random wirings on the early model with one unit per KC, Hallem's receptor data as the input for the weak odors, a 130 Hz per-claw threshold followed by a cap. Each is on an earlier model and carries a different error, not a smaller one, than the breadth-2 fit's, and scaling APL's inhibition of the PN boutons is not among them. The test for each was the one the profile was put to, in the best family: whether it lowers the common error on the real wiring and on re-drawn ones without adding as much error elsewhere. What it has to change is known in outline: on raw counts the model has the distances among those six esters about right with APL off and too small with APL on, and, counted above 1 z, the KCs that respond to four to seven odors carry too much of the overlap between odors with APL on ([above](#apl-effect-by-class)). No change of the input screened in the best family does this, on the real wiring or carried over to re-drawn ones, and only about two fifths of the common error is in the geometry that the two conditions share; what is left on APL's side is what neither experiment tried: scores fitted directly in simulation on several wirings at once (single-glomerulus changes do not add up, so a profile found through them need not be the best one) and inhibition that depends on the odor otherwise than by growing with a bouton's or a claw's own input, the form that was emulated and did not help. The two changes at the cell site that raised the block under the readout to the flies' on the real wiring have not been run on a re-drawn wiring; that run would say whether a block made through which KCs respond, the carrier listed above, holds in the best family or belongs to the hemibrain wiring. Each of these states its target against all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) and against the six that are alike, because the test on split halves of the recordings failed through the other two; the two have since been found stronger and not different, so the mean over all eight is the target and the six are given beside it ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). And the firing ceiling's case for the base model has its like-for-like number: as a mean over four wirings read through the trial noise, the family with the ceiling is level on raw counts with the family without it, so that the case rests on single wirings, on the model without noise and on realism. From the data side of the main target ([above](#data-side)), which the response criterion of the realism bands ([footnote](#fn-baseline-noise-units)) had left to measure: which unit the flies' side of the target is held to, the recordings' z-scored values, as elsewhere on this page, or baseline-noise units, the unit of the realism bands, with the mean over all the recordings with APL output blocked (TNT) in either case (the choice moves the mean part of [the APL-effect loss](#apl-effect) and nothing else, so until it is made the families are ranked on the pattern part and the mean part is given against both effects; if the target stays on the z-scored values, the mean part is nearly closed for the family with the firing ceiling and the pattern part is what remains; if it moves to baseline-noise units, the mean part is open again for every model, by {{diff:data:noise_apl_effect_mean -- E76/fits.csv:nu_rate0.068_aplbothdnu_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2:spike_counts_cosine__apl_effect_mean ~ .3f}} for the best family fitted to that effect and by more through the trial noise); for that case, a KC response that grows with the KC's breadth, the mechanism or term of the readout listed above from the per-KC normalization of the recordings, as the way to a larger mean effect that is not more responses with APL off, the route that the fit to the effect in baseline-noise units took at a cost on the pattern and toward the edge of the band on the ratio of the response rates (if a model gets the growth inside the realism bands, the mean part closes without that cost; if it does not, the mean part stays open in those units for this family; read since without simulation, the growth alone does not close it, weighting the best fit's spike counts by the KC's breadth moving its mean effect by {{diff:E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p_is_flies=True;target=noise:mean -- E80/breadth_weighted.csv:tag=nu_rate0.068_aplboth_refr3_adapt0.1114t1000_k2;p=0.0;target=noise:mean ~ +.3f}} at most: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates)); the split of the effect by odors per KC reported in both units for every later fit; and the state of the two strongest recordings, in which blocking APL output brings the pairs among 2h, IaA, pa, eb, ep and ms far closer than in the other six, as a target of its own for the mechanisms that change what reaches the KCs (the fixed changes of the input screened in the input side of the error common to all wirings, [above](#input-side), were scored against all eight recordings and against the six, not against the two, and none lowered the common error; the high per-claw knee without a dead zone, [above](#claw-knee), was scored in the same way, and where it lowers the ester group's error, with little or nothing passed below the knee, the pattern part is higher), since neither a weaker APL nor a shifted threshold makes that state in the model. The readout itself stays as it is, with no measurement noise, one-spike floor or membrane-potential term. From the input side of the error common to all wirings ([above](#input-side)): the common error stays the target, and the handles on the input that were screened are closed for this family. None lowers it, an input searched within a factor of two fits the real wiring's own remainder and not what the wirings share, and the weak odors' input stays the lab's, since neither Hallem's receptor data nor the searched input helps the best family. Of the changes to what reaches the KCs, the high per-claw knee without a dead zone was not among the handles and has been run since ([above](#claw-knee)): it holds the pairs with near-identical ORN input apart only with a dead zone that silences ms and B-myr, and the per-claw transfer is closed for this family on the main target. Nor does the comparison's definition make the common error: against the six recordings that are alike and against the effect in baseline-noise units it is as large ([the data side of the main target](#data-side)). What else is left to propose lies outside what was screened: how APL's inhibition unfolds in time and adapts, differences between types of KCs, and inhibition that depends on the odor otherwise than by growing with a bouton's or a claw's own input (of these, the length of the odor pulse, thresholds that differ between the two conditions as an adaptation to the block would leave them, the types of KCs and each odor's recruitment have since been run on the real wiring, and none lowers the common error: [the flies' pulse in the model and the remaining candidates for the common error](#remaining-candidates); APL's time constant has been run as well and does not lower it: [the flies' recording protocol in the model](#flies-protocol)).
