**What changes in the flies' values.** The overall response rates hardly depend on the unit. The control flies' is the same by construction; with APL output blocked (TNT) it is a little higher in baseline-noise units, and the ratio with it, well inside the unchanged band on the ratio. The per-odor response rates keep their order: across the 16 odors the rates by the two criteria correlate at ρ={{data:noise_ctrl_frac_rho_vs_z ~ .2f}} in control flies and {{data:noise_tnt_frac_rho_vs_z ~ .2f}} with APL output blocked (TNT), so a model's response rate ρ changes little. What changes is how the responses are spread over the KCs: in baseline-noise units more KCs respond to nothing and more respond to eight or more odors, in both genotypes, and fewer respond to between one and three. The band on odors per KC is a little narrower with APL on and wider with APL off. Outside the realism bands, the response rates of the flies given on this page (overall, per odor, and in every response rate ρ of a table) remain by the recordings' own criterion, by which the experiments were run and scored.

**Caveats.** The baseline noise has been computed only for the recordings of this odor panel, those behind the two KC matrices; the other KC recordings this page refers to (the low-concentration panels, the wild-type recordings) are still in their own units, and no band uses them. A baseline-noise unit is not a unit of activity: the signal is not divided by a resting fluorescence, so a response in these units still depends on how bright a KC is, and the KCs that respond to many odors are the brighter ones on average; the baseline noise itself is no larger in those KCs than in the ones that respond to nothing, and does not differ between the genotypes by more than the recordings differ among themselves. Spikes and noise-normalized fluorescence are both fixed units but not the same unit: what ties them is the calibration at the control flies' response rate, at that one point, and the flies' responses are counted through measurement noise where the models' are not. The main target is not touched by any of this: the flies' odor-odor distances, and with them the per-pair APL effect and its floor, are computed from the recordings' z-scored values as before. Whether they too should be taken in baseline-noise units is a separate question, measured in [the data side of the main target](#data-side) and not yet decided: in these units the flies' mean APL effect is larger and its pattern across pairs is the same.

### How a model's pattern error is split into what it inherits from its distances with APL off {#fn-inherited-split}

**What is done.** Distances are taken as similarities, one minus the distance. On each side, the flies' and the model's, one curve is fitted across the 120 pairs that gives a pair's similarity with APL on from its similarity with APL off: a power curve, the similarity with APL off raised to a power and multiplied by a factor, both found by least squares. A curve gives every pair an APL effect from its similarity with APL off alone. A pair's error, the model's APL effect minus the flies', is then exactly the sum of three terms. The inherited term is the effect that the flies' curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect it gives at the flies' own: the error the model would have if it followed the flies' curve without departures. The curve term is the effect that the model's curve gives at the model's similarity with APL off minus the effect that the flies' curve gives there. The departures are the model's departure from its own curve on that pair minus the flies' departure from theirs. With each term's mean over the pairs removed, a term's share is its sum of products with the pattern error divided by the pattern error's squared sum; the three shares add to one, and a share is negative when its term offsets the others.

**Why this split.** A change of the input changes a pair's distance in both conditions. Where a model's distances with APL on follow its curve, such a change moves a pair along the curve, and the error it reaches in this way is the inherited term. The curve term belongs to how strongly APL separates pairs at a given similarity, and the departures to what APL does to particular pairs, the block among them. The split says where an error lies, not what causes it, and it is not a bound: an input set freely for every glomerulus of every odor also moves a wiring's departures, as the search on the real wiring did.

**How far it depends on the curve.** The flies' curve was also fitted leaving out each odor's pairs in turn, a pair taking the mean of its two odors' left-out curves, and on a random half of the recordings of each genotype, a hundred times. For the mean over the eight wirings the inherited share is {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=loo:share_inherited ~ .0%}} with the left-out curves, against {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=cal;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}} with the curve fitted to all pairs, and between {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q05:value ~ .0%}} and {{E77/report_scalars.csv:inherited_halves_cal_q95:value ~ .0%}} over the halves (the middle 90 % of them). On raw spike counts it is {{E77/inherited_parts.csv:folder=E72 members;tag=mean8;readout=raw;target=z8;data_curve_fit=insample:share_inherited ~ .0%}}. The power curve has two parameters, and no other family of curves was tried.

### How the APL calyx maps were analysed, predicted from the connectomes and scored {#fn-calyx-maps}

**The measured maps.** A recording holds one map per presentation, the mean of five frames around the peak of the response as a change over the baseline fluorescence, in blocks of three presentations: the solvent, then one odor at one concentration twice; one block is the solvent three times. A stimulus's map is the mean of its two presentations, each minus a solvent map. The solvent map was taken in three ways: the presentation at the same position within the solvent-only block, which is the baseline of the statistics of the measured maps in the text; the mean of all solvent presentations, which is the baseline of the comparison with the predicted maps (the first gives the same there); and the mean of the solvent presentations that open the blocks. The reliability of the maps, the likeness of different odors' maps and the direction of pa's shift against ms hold under each. Correlations between maps are over the pixels inside the calyx outline after a Gaussian smoothing of 2 pixels. The pattern common to a recording's stimuli is the first singular vector of its stimulus × pixel matrix, and the remainder of a map is the map without its part along that pattern. The remainder's statistics are over each odor's two highest concentrations, and its length is the distance at which the cross-correlation between the remainders of the two presentations falls to 1/e, which leaves out the noise that the presentations do not share. For the positions of two odors' responses, a recording's two concentrations are those at which the mean responses over the calyx are closest, among maps with a positive mean and a correlation between presentations of 0.5 or more; a fly's two hemispheres are averaged, and the intervals are from 10,000 resamplings of the flies.

**The predicted maps.** For an odor, each PN bouton of a calyx contributes its number of release sites times the evoked PN rate of its glomerulus, at the bouton's centre, in a view from posterior with dorsal up; a calyx of the other side than the recording is mirrored first. The axes of the four connectome data sets were set and checked from landmarks: the lobes anterior of the calyx, the tip of the vertical lobe and the calyx dorsal of the peduncle, the tip of the medial lobe medial of the calyx. Maps were made for slabs 6 µm thick along the anterior–posterior axis, one every 3 µm, and for the whole calyx, with a Gaussian smoothing of 2, 4 or 8 µm, inside an outline that holds 97.5 % of APL's synapses in the slab. Predicted and measured maps were sampled on a 12 × 12 grid over the bounding boxes of their outlines, with each odor's map divided by its mean before a difference was taken, and scored as the Pearson correlation over the grid cells inside both outlines, with the measured image as recorded, mirrored left to right, turned upside down, and both. For a measured difference the two concentrations are the strongest pair whose mean responses are within a factor of 1.25 of each other, among responses of at least a quarter of the odor's largest. The null permutes the glomerulus labels of the vector of PN rates, 1,000 times, with the same permutations for every slab, smoothing and recording, and takes the best over orientations, slabs and smoothings for each permutation as for the prediction. Three alternatives to the boutons were scored in the same way: the claws (each claw at its position, weighted by its number of PN synapses and the rate of its PN's glomerulus), the KCs' spikes (the KCs' synapses onto APL in the calyx, weighted by the KC's spike count in the breadth-2 APL-effect fit with APL on; hemibrain only) and the anatomy alone (the synapses between PNs and APL, unweighted; for the single-odor maps only, since it predicts no difference between odors). In the FlyWire and BANC tables a bouton's weight is its number of synaptic connections and not of release sites, which changes the weights within a calyx only if the number of connections per release site differs between boutons, and the calyx regions of the male CNS leave out the posterior part of the calyx.

**The co-localization proxy.** The inhibition of a glomerulus for an odor is either the same for all glomeruli, a strength times the odor's mean PN rate, or its local field, the PN rates of all glomeruli weighted by their co-localization with it, scaled so that the mean inhibition over odors and glomeruli is the same under both rules; negative evoked rates are set to zero. Subtractive inhibition takes the inhibition from the rate, with a floor at zero (strengths 0.5 and 1), and divisive inhibition divides the rate by one plus the inhibition over the mean rate (strengths 1 and 4). The proxy of a pair is its cosine distance under the local rule minus that under the global one. For a setting, the proxy, with its mean over the pairs removed, is multiplied by one factor fitted by least squares to the common error on the 105 pairs among 15 odors, and what is left of the common error on the 15 pairs of the left-out odor is summed, as squares, over the 16 odors; the share removed is one minus that sum over the common error's squared sum. The null permutes the glomeruli of the co-localization matrix, rows and columns together, 1,000 times, for each setting and for the best of all settings in each permutation. The test asked for 15 % or more removed on left-out odors, at or above the 95th percentile of the null.
